at lade.explanation: "At lade" means "to let". To say you leave something as it is, use it too: "Jeg lader nøglen ligge" (I leave the key lying there).

sentence.da: Mor vil ikke **lade** os gå alene.
sentence.en: Mom won't let us go alone.

at lade som om.explanation: "At lade som om" means "to pretend". It is built from "at lade" (to let) and "som om" (as if). To say what someone pretends, say: "Han lader som om han sover" (He pretends he is sleeping).

sentence.da: Børnene vil **lade som om** de er pirater.
sentence.en: The children want to pretend they are pirates.

at lade være.explanation: "At lade være" means "to refrain". To name what you refrain from, add "med at" (with to) and a verb: "Jeg lader være med at ryge" (I refrain from smoking). To tell someone to stop, say: "Lad være!" (Don't!).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **lade være** med at spise slik.
sentence.en: I will refrain from eating candy.

at lande.explanation: "At lande" means "to land". The noun is "en landing" (a landing). For example, "en blød landing" (a soft landing).

sentence.da: Flyet skal **lande** om en time.
sentence.en: The plane will land in an hour.

at lappe.explanation: "At lappe" means "to patch or mend". The piece you put over the hole is "en lap" (a patch).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **lappe** hullet i cykelslangen i aften.
sentence.en: I have to patch the hole in the bike tube tonight.

at larme.explanation: "At larme" means "to make noise". To tell someone to stop, say: "Hold op med at larme!" (Stop making noise!).

sentence.da: Børnene må ikke **larme** efter klokken ti.
sentence.en: The children must not make noise after ten o'clock.

at lave.explanation: "At lave" means "to make or to do". To say you make something, say: "Jeg laver en kage" (I am making a cake). To ask what someone is busy with, say: "Hvad laver du?" (What are you doing?).

forms.en: I have made / I have done

sentence.da: Hvad skal vi **lave** i aften?
sentence.en: What are we going to do tonight?

at lave en fejl.explanation: "At lave en fejl" means "to make a mistake". To talk about mistakes in general, drop "en": "Alle laver fejl" (Everyone makes mistakes).

sentence.da: Jeg er bange for at **lave en fejl**.
sentence.en: I am afraid of making a mistake.

at lave lektier.explanation: "At lave lektier" means "to do homework". Danish says "lave" (make) where English says "do". To ask if someone has finished, say: "Har du lavet dine lektier?" (Have you done your homework?).

sentence.da: Børnene skal **lave lektier** nu.
sentence.en: The children have to do homework now.

at lave mad.explanation: "At lave mad" means "to cook". It is built from "lave" (to make) and "mad" (food), so literally it is "to make food". To say what you cook, drop "mad": "Jeg laver pasta" (I am making pasta).

sentence.da: Min far vil **lave mad** i aften.
sentence.en: My father will cook tonight.

at lave om.explanation: "At lave om" means "to change or redo". To say you change a plan, add "på" (on): "Jeg laver om på planen" (I am changing the plan).

sentence.da: Hun skal **lave om** på hele rapporten.
sentence.en: She has to change the whole report.

at lave sjov.explanation: "At lave sjov" means "to joke around". To say someone teases you, add "med" (with): "Hun laver sjov med mig" (She is teasing me).

sentence.da: Min bror elsker at **lave sjov**, og alle griner.
sentence.en: My brother loves to joke around, and everyone laughs.

at le.explanation: "At le" means "to laugh". To say you laugh at someone, add "af" (at): "Han ler af mig" (He is laughing at me).

sentence.da: Børnene vil **le** af den sjove film.
sentence.en: The children want to laugh at the funny movie.

at lede.explanation: "At lede" means "to search or lead". To say someone leads a team, say: "Hun leder holdet" (She leads the team). To say you search for something, add "efter" (for): "Vi leder efter en ny lejlighed" (We are looking for a new apartment).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **lede** efter min hat.
sentence.en: I have to look for my hat.

at lede efter.explanation: "At lede efter" means "to look for". To say you look at something you can already see, use "at se på" (to look at): "Jeg ser på billedet" (I am looking at the picture).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **lede efter** mine nøgler.
sentence.en: I want to look for my keys.

at legalisere.explanation: "At legalisere" means "to legalize". To say you have a document confirmed as official, say: "at legalisere et dokument" (to have a document certified).

sentence.da: Nogle lande vil **legalisere** cannabis til medicinsk brug.
sentence.en: Some countries want to legalize cannabis for medical use.

at lege.explanation: "At lege" means "to play". For sports and instruments, use "at spille" (to play): "Han spiller fodbold" (He plays soccer).

sentence.da: Børnene vil **lege** med bolden i haven.
sentence.en: The children want to play with the ball in the garden.

at legitimere.explanation: "At legitimere" means "to legitimize or show ID". To say you show who you are, add "sig" (yourself): "Du skal legitimere dig i banken" (You must show ID at the bank).

sentence.da: Du skal **legitimere** dig med pas eller kørekort.
sentence.en: You must show ID with a passport or driver's license.

at leje.explanation: "At leje" means "to rent". To say you rent something out to someone else, use "at udleje" (to rent out): "Vi udlejer lejligheden" (We are renting out the apartment).

sentence.da: Vi vil **leje** en bil i weekenden.
sentence.en: We want to rent a car for the weekend.

at lempe.explanation: "At lempe" means "to ease or relax (rules)". To say a requirement becomes less strict, say: "lempe kravene" (ease the requirements).

sentence.da: Regeringen vil **lempe** reglerne for rejser til udlandet.
sentence.en: The government will relax the rules for travel abroad.

at lette.explanation: "At lette" means "to take off". To say something makes a task easier, use it too: "Det letter arbejdet" (That makes the work easier).

sentence.da: Flyet skal **lette** om fem minutter.
sentence.en: The plane takes off in five minutes.

at leve.explanation: "At leve" means "to live (be alive)". To say someone is still alive, say: "Hun lever stadig" (She is still alive). To say where your home is, use "at bo" (to live somewhere): "Jeg bor i Aarhus" (I live in Aarhus).

sentence.da: Fisk kan ikke **leve** uden vand.
sentence.en: Fish cannot live without water.

at lide.explanation: "At lide" means "to suffer". To say what someone suffers from, add "af" (from): "Han lider af hovedpine" (He suffers from headaches). Do not mix it up with "kan lide" (like). For example, "Jeg kan lide kaffe" (I like coffee).

sentence.da: Dyrene vil **lide**, når der ikke er mere vand.
sentence.en: The animals will suffer when there is no more water.

at ligge.explanation: "At ligge" means "to lie (be lying)". To say where something is lying, say: "Bogen ligger på bordet" (The book is lying on the table). To say where a place is located, say: "Byen ligger ved havet" (The town is by the sea). Do not mix it up with "at lægge" (to put something down): "Jeg lægger bogen på bordet" (I put the book on the table).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **ligge** i sengen og sove.
sentence.en: I want to lie in bed and sleep.

at ligge syg.explanation: "At ligge syg" means "to be ill in bed". To say you are sick without lying in bed, use "at være syg" (to be sick): "Jeg er syg i dag" (I am sick today).

forms.en: I have been ill in bed

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **ligge syg** hele ugen.
sentence.en: I cannot lie in bed sick all week.

at ligne.explanation: "At ligne" means "to look like". To say someone resembles a person, say: "Drengen ligner sin far" (The boy looks like his father). To say how someone appears, use "at se ud" (to look): "Du ser træt ud" (You look tired).

sentence.da: Hun kan **ligne** sin mor, når hun smiler.
sentence.en: She can look like her mother when she smiles.

at like.explanation: "At like" means "to like (online)". To say she likes a post, say: "Hun liker alle mine opslag" (She likes all my posts). For a person or food, use "at kunne lide" (to like): "Jeg kan lide pizza" (I like pizza).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **like** dit billede på Instagram.
sentence.en: I want to like your picture on Instagram.

at lindre.explanation: "At lindre" means "to relieve". To say a pill eases pain, say: "Tabletten lindrer hovedpinen" (The pill relieves the headache).

sentence.da: Varme kan **lindre** smerten i ryggen.
sentence.en: Heat can relieve the pain in the back.

at logge ind.explanation: "At logge ind" means "to log in". To say you forgot the code you need, say: "Jeg har glemt min adgangskode" (I have forgotten my password).

sentence.da: Du skal **logge ind** for at se dine beskeder.
sentence.en: You have to log in to see your messages.

at logge ud.explanation: "At logge ud" means "to log out". It is built from "at logge" (to log) and "ud" (out). To remind someone, say: "Husk at logge ud!" (Remember to log out!).

sentence.da: Du skal **logge ud** på en fælles computer.
sentence.en: You should log out on a shared computer.

at lokalisere.explanation: "At lokalisere" means "to locate". To say someone found out where something is, name the thing found: "Politiet lokaliserede bilen" (The police located the car).

sentence.da: Teknikeren kan **lokalisere** fejlen på få minutter.
sentence.en: The technician can locate the fault in a few minutes.

at lokke.explanation: "At lokke" means "to lure or tempt". To say you get someone to come along, add "med" (along): "Jeg lokkede ham med" (I lured him along).

sentence.da: Duften af brød kan **lokke** folk ind i butikken.
sentence.en: The smell of bread can lure people into the store.

at love.explanation: "At love" means "to promise". To say you promise to do something, add "at" (to) and a verb: "Jeg lover at komme" (I promise to come). To say you promise a person a thing, put the person first: "Han lovede mig en gave" (He promised me a gift).

sentence.da: Kan du **love** mig, at du kommer i morgen?
sentence.en: Can you promise me that you will come tomorrow?

at lovgive.explanation: "At lovgive" means "to legislate". It is built from "en lov" (a law) and "at give" (to give). In Denmark, the parliament that makes the laws is "Folketinget" (the Danish parliament).

sentence.da: Politikerne kan **lovgive** om, hvem der må køre bil.
sentence.en: The politicians can legislate about who may drive a car.

at lufte hunden.explanation: "At lufte hunden" means "to walk the dog". It is built from "at lufte" (to air) and "hunden" (the dog). To ask someone to do it, say: "Kan du lufte hunden?" (Can you walk the dog?)

sentence.da: Hver morgen skal jeg **lufte hunden** i parken.
sentence.en: Every morning I have to walk the dog in the park.

at lufte ud.explanation: "At lufte ud" means "to air out". The small word "ud" (out) also appears in "at gå ud" (to go out) and "at hælde ud" (to pour out). To remind someone to open a window, say: "Husk at lufte ud i soveværelset" (Remember to air out the bedroom).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **lufte ud**, fordi der lugter dårligt her.
sentence.en: I want to air out because it smells bad in here.

at luge.explanation: "At luge" means "to weed". To say what you pull out, add "ukrudt" (weeds): "Jeg lugede ukrudt i haven" (I pulled weeds in the garden).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **luge** bedet, så blomsterne kan vokse.
sentence.en: I will weed the bed so the flowers can grow.

at lugte.explanation: "At lugte" means "to smell", both giving off a smell and noticing one. To say how something smells, add "godt" (good) or "dårligt" (bad): "Det lugter godt" (It smells good). To say what it smells of, add "af" (of): "Rummet lugter af røg" (The room smells of smoke).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **lugte** kaffe fra køkkenet.
sentence.en: I can smell coffee from the kitchen.

at lukke.explanation: "At lukke" means "to close". To say a shop shuts at a certain time, add the time: "Vi lukker om ti minutter" (We close in ten minutes).

sentence.da: Kan du **lukke** vinduet? Det er koldt.
sentence.en: Can you close the window? It is cold.

at lyde.explanation: "At lyde" means "to sound". To say how an idea or plan seems to you, add an adjective: "Det lyder godt" (That sounds good). Do not mix it up with "at høre" (to hear), which is for noticing a noise. For example, "Jeg hører musik" (I hear music).

sentence.da: Det kan **lyde** som en god idé.
sentence.en: It may sound like a good idea.

at lykkes.explanation: "At lykkes" means "to succeed". It goes with "det" (it) and the person who succeeds, such as "mig" (me). For example, "Det lykkedes mig at finde den" (I succeeded in finding it).

sentence.da: Jeg håber, det vil **lykkes** mig at finde et job.
sentence.en: I hope I will succeed in finding a job.

at lyne.explanation: "At lyne" means "to flash with lightning". It always goes with "det" (it), like "it" in English weather talk. For example, "Det lyner" (There is lightning).

sentence.da: Himlen er mørk, og det vil snart **lyne**.
sentence.en: The sky is dark, and there will soon be lightning.

at lyne op.explanation: "At lyne op" means "to unzip". The small word "op" (up) also appears in "at knappe op" (to unbutton) and "at låse op" (to unlock). To say you open your jacket because you are warm, say: "Jeg lyner jakken op, fordi jeg har det varmt" (I unzip my jacket because I am hot).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **lyne op**, når lynlåsen sidder fast.
sentence.en: I cannot unzip when the zipper is stuck.

at lyse.explanation: "At lyse" means "to shine or light". To say a light source gives light, name it: "Månen lyser" (The moon is shining). To say you point light at something, add "på" (on): "Jeg lyste på døren med lommelygten" (I shone the flashlight on the door).

sentence.da: Lampen skal **lyse** i mørket.
sentence.en: The lamp has to shine in the dark.

at lyse op.explanation: "At lyse op" means "to light up". It is built from "at lyse" (to shine) and "op" (up). To say a lamp lights a room, put the room before "op": "Lampen lyser rummet op" (The lamp lights up the room).

sentence.da: Hendes ansigt vil **lyse op**, når hun ser dig.
sentence.en: Her face will light up when she sees you.

at lytte.explanation: "At lytte" means "to listen". To say what you listen to, add "til" (to): "Jeg lyttede til musikken" (I listened to the music). Do not mix it up with "at høre" (to hear), which is for noticing a sound without trying. For example, "Jeg hørte en lyd" (I heard a sound).

sentence.da: Du skal **lytte**, når læreren taler.
sentence.en: You have to listen when the teacher talks.

at lytte til.explanation: "At lytte til" means "to listen to". The thing you listen to comes after "til" (to). For example, "Jeg lytter til radioen" (I listen to the radio). Do not mix it up with "at høre" (to hear), which is for noticing a sound. For another example, "Jeg hørte dig ikke" (I did not hear you).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **lytte til** musik i aften.
sentence.en: I want to listen to music tonight.

at lyve.explanation: "At lyve" means "to lie", as in telling a lie. To tell someone they are not telling the truth, say: "Du lyver!" (You are lying!) Do not mix it up with "at ligge" (to lie down), which is for being in a flat position: "Jeg ligger i sengen" (I am lying in bed).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **lyve** for mig.
sentence.en: You must not lie to me.

at låne.explanation: "At låne" means "to borrow or lend". To ask to borrow something, say: "Kan jeg låne din pen?" (Can I borrow your pen?) To make clear that you lend something, add "ud" (out): "Jeg låner min cykel ud til hende" (I lend my bike out to her).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **låne** en bog på biblioteket.
sentence.en: I want to borrow a book at the library.

at låse.explanation: "At låse" means "to lock". To say someone locks a bike, say: "Han låser cyklen" (He locks the bike). To say you unlock something, add "op" (up): "Jeg låser skabet op" (I unlock the cabinet).

sentence.da: Husk at **låse** døren, når du går.
sentence.en: Remember to lock the door when you leave.

at låse op.explanation: "At låse op" means "to unlock". It is built from "at låse" (to lock) and "op" (up). When something is being unlocked, "op" goes at the end: "Hun låser skabet op" (She unlocks the cabinet).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **låse op**, fordi jeg har glemt nøglen.
sentence.en: I cannot unlock because I have forgotten the key.

at lægge.explanation: "At lægge" means "to lay down". To say you put a person or thing somewhere flat, add the place: "Jeg lægger barnet i sengen" (I put the baby in bed). Do not mix it up with "at ligge" (to be lying somewhere), which has no object. For example, "Bogen ligger på bordet" (The book is lying on the table).

sentence.da: Du skal **lægge** tøjet i skabet.
sentence.en: You have to put the clothes in the closet.

at lægge fra sig.explanation: "At lægge fra sig" means "to put down". The last word changes with the person. To say "he" put something down, use "sig" (himself): "Han lagde bogen fra sig" (He put the book down). To say "I" did, use "mig" (myself): "Jeg lagde bogen fra mig" (I put the book down).

sentence.da: Hun skal **lægge fra sig** det, hun har i hænderne.
sentence.en: She has to put down what she has in her hands.

at lægge mærke til.explanation: "At lægge mærke til" means "to notice". Literally, it is "to put a mark to". To say you noticed a detail, say: "Jeg lagde mærke til hans nye jakke" (I noticed his new jacket).

sentence.da: Hun vil nok **lægge mærke til** din nye frisure.
sentence.en: She will probably notice your new haircut.

at lægge planer.explanation: "At lægge planer" means "to make plans". Literally, it is "to lay plans". To say you plan one thing, use "at planlægge" (to plan): "Jeg planlægger turen" (I am planning the trip).

sentence.da: Vi vil **lægge planer** for sommeren.
sentence.en: We want to make plans for the summer.

at lægge på.explanation: "At lægge på" means "to hang up". Literally, it is "to lay on". To say someone ends a phone call, say: "Hun lagde på uden at sige farvel" (She hung up without saying goodbye).

sentence.da: Jeg må **lægge på**, fordi bussen kommer.
sentence.en: I have to hang up because the bus is coming.

at lægge sammen.explanation: "At lægge sammen" means "to add up". It is built from "at lægge" (to put) and "sammen" (together). To say you add numbers, name them before "sammen": "Jeg lægger to og tre sammen" (I add two and three together).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **lægge sammen** i hovedet.
sentence.en: I can add up in my head.

at lægge sig.explanation: "At lægge sig" means "to lie down". The word "sig" (oneself) changes with the person. To say you lie down on the sofa, say: "Jeg lægger mig på sofaen" (I lie down on the sofa). To say you are already lying there, use "at ligge" (to lie): "Jeg ligger i sengen" (I am lying in bed).

sentence.da: Han er træt og vil **lægge sig** på sofaen.
sentence.en: He is tired and wants to lie down on the sofa.

at lægge vægt på.explanation: "At lægge vægt på" means "to emphasize". Literally, it is "to put weight on". To say what you find important, put it after "på" (on): "Vi lægger vægt på kvalitet" (We emphasize quality).

sentence.da: Skolen vil **lægge vægt på**, at børnene får frisk luft.
sentence.en: The school wants to emphasize that the children get fresh air.

at lække.explanation: "At lække" means "to leak". To say secret information gets out, use it for the information: "Nogen lækkede dokumentet" (Someone leaked the document).

sentence.da: Taget begynder at **lække**, når det regner meget.
sentence.en: The roof starts to leak when it rains a lot.

at læne sig.explanation: "At læne sig" means "to lean". The word "sig" (oneself) changes with the person, such as "mig" (myself). To say you lean against a wall, say: "Jeg læner mig mod væggen" (I lean against the wall).

sentence.da: Han vil **læne sig** tilbage og slappe af.
sentence.en: He wants to lean back and relax.

at lære.explanation: "At lære" means "to learn or teach". To say you learn a subject, name it: "Jeg lærer dansk" (I learn Danish). To say you teach a person, put the person first and the subject last: "Hun lærer mig dansk" (She teaches me Danish). Do not mix it up with "at læse" (to read). For example, "Jeg læser en bog" (I am reading a book).

sentence.da: Børn kan **lære** meget i skolen.
sentence.en: Children can learn a lot at school.

at lære at kende.explanation: "At lære at kende" means "to get to know". To say you are getting to know a person, put the person in the middle, after "lære" (learn): "Jeg lærer ham at kende" (I am getting to know him).

forms.da: jeg har lært ham at kende
forms.en: I have gotten to know him

sentence.da: Det er dejligt at **lære at kende** nye mennesker.
sentence.en: It is nice to get to know new people.

at lære udenad.explanation: "At lære udenad" means "to memorize". It is built from "at lære" (to learn) and "udenad" (by heart). To say you memorize words, say: "Jeg lærer ordene udenad" (I memorize the words).

sentence.da: Eleverne skal **lære udenad** til prøven i morgen.
sentence.en: The students have to memorize for the test tomorrow.

at læse.explanation: "At læse" means "to read". To say you read a book, say: "Jeg læser en bog" (I am reading a book). To say you study a subject at university, name the subject: "Hun læser medicin" (She studies medicine). Do not mix it up with "at lære" (to learn). For example, "Jeg lærer dansk" (I am learning Danish).

sentence.da: Min datter kan **læse** og skrive.
sentence.en: My daughter can read and write.

at læse om.explanation: "At læse om" means "to read about". To say what you read about, put the topic after "om" (about): "Jeg læser om dansk historie" (I am reading about Danish history). To say you read a book itself, leave out "om" and use "at læse" (to read): "Jeg læser en bog" (I am reading a book).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **læse om** Island.
sentence.en: I would like to read about Iceland.

at læse op.explanation: "At læse op" means "to read aloud". To say someone reads aloud to a group, add "for" (for) and the group: "Læreren læser op for klassen" (The teacher reads aloud to the class). To say someone reads out a list, put the list before "op": "Han læste navnene op" (He read out the names).

sentence.da: Kan du **læse op** for os?
sentence.en: Can you read aloud to us?

at læse til.explanation: "At læse til" means "to study to become". To say which job, put it after "til" (to): "Han læser til læge" (He is studying to become a doctor). Without "til", "at læse" (to read) can mean "to study" a subject. For example, "Hun læser medicin" (She studies medicine).

sentence.da: Min søster vil **læse til** læge i København.
sentence.en: My sister wants to study to become a doctor in Copenhagen.

at løbe.explanation: "At løbe" means "to run". To say you run as exercise, say: "Jeg løber hver morgen" (I run every morning). To say a nose is running, say: "Min næse løber" (My nose is running). To say you have none left of something, use "at løbe tør for" (to run out of): "Vi løb tør for mælk" (We ran out of milk).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **løbe** hurtigt for at nå bussen.
sentence.en: I want to run fast to catch the bus.

at løbe efter.explanation: "At løbe efter" means "to run after". To say a dog runs behind a ball, put the ball after "efter" (after): "Hunden løber efter bolden" (The dog runs after the ball). Do not mix it up with "at jage" (to chase), which is for hunting down a target. For example, "Katten jager musen" (The cat chases the mouse).

sentence.da: Jeg måtte **løbe efter** bussen i morges.
sentence.en: I had to run after the bus this morning.

at løbe en tur.explanation: "At løbe en tur" means "to go for a run". To say you run after work, say: "Jeg løber en tur efter arbejde" (I go for a run after work). The words "en tur" (a trip) also appear in "at gå en tur" (to go for a walk).

forms.en: I have gone for a run

related.en: to go for a bike ride

sentence.da: Når solen skinner, vil jeg **løbe en tur**.
sentence.en: When the sun shines, I want to go for a run.

at løbe ind i.explanation: "At løbe ind i" means "to run into". To say you bump into something by accident, say: "Jeg løb ind i en dør" (I ran into a door). To say you meet someone by chance, say: "Jeg løb ind i min nabo" (I ran into my neighbor).

sentence.da: I byen kan jeg **løbe ind i** en gammel ven.
sentence.en: In town I might run into an old friend.

at løbe på skøjter.explanation: "At løbe på skøjter" means "to ice-skate". It is built from "at løbe" (to run) and "på skøjter" (on skates), so it is literally "to run on skates".

sentence.da: Om vinteren kan vi **løbe på skøjter** på isen.
sentence.en: In winter we can ice-skate on the ice.

at løbe tør for.explanation: "At løbe tør for" means "to run out of". Literally, it is "to run dry for". To say what ran out, put it after "for" (for): "Vi løb tør for mælk" (We ran out of milk).

sentence.da: Bilen kan **løbe tør for** benzin på vejen.
sentence.en: The car can run out of gas on the road.

at løbe væk.explanation: "At løbe væk" means "to run away". To say what someone runs away from, add "fra" (from): "Drengen løb væk fra hunden" (The boy ran away from the dog).

sentence.da: Barnet må ikke **løbe væk** fra os.
sentence.en: The child must not run away from us.

at løfte.explanation: "At løfte" means "to lift". To say you lift a person or thing, name it: "Jeg løfter barnet" (I lift the child). To say you raise a body part, name it: "Hun løfter armen" (She raises her arm). Do not mix it up with "et løfte" (a promise), which is a noun. For example, "Jeg giver dig et løfte" (I give you a promise).

sentence.da: Han kan **løfte** tunge ting alene.
sentence.en: He can lift heavy things alone.

at løse.explanation: "At løse" means "to solve". To say you solve a task, say: "Jeg løser opgaven" (I solve the task). To say you untie something, say: "Hun løste knuden" (She untied the knot).

sentence.da: Vi kan **løse** problemet sammen.
sentence.en: We can solve the problem together.

at løslade.explanation: "At løslade" means "to release", as in letting a person out of prison. It is built from "løs" (loose) and "at lade" (to let). To say a person was released, use "blive løsladt" (to be released): "Han blev løsladt i går" (He was released yesterday).

sentence.da: Efter to år i fængsel vil de **løslade** ham.
sentence.en: After two years in prison, they will release him.

en ladcykel.explanation: "En ladcykel" means "a cargo bike". It is built from "lad" (cargo bed) and "en cykel" (a bike). To say you take the children to school by cargo bike, say: "Jeg kører børnene i skole på ladcyklen" (I take the children to school on the cargo bike).

sentence.da: Der er plads til mange indkøb i min **ladcykel**.
sentence.en: There is room for a lot of groceries in my cargo bike.

en lade.explanation: "En lade" means "a barn". Do not mix it up with "at lade" (to let), which is spelled the same. For example, "Jeg lader dig gå" (I let you go).

sentence.da: Bonden har hø og maskiner i sin **lade**.
sentence.en: The farmer keeps hay and machines in his barn.

en ladestander.explanation: "En ladestander" means "a charging station". It is built from "at lade" (to charge) and "en stander" (a stand).

sentence.da: Jeg parkerer ved en **ladestander** og lader min bil.
sentence.en: I park at a charging station and charge my car.

en lagerarbejder.explanation: "En lagerarbejder" means "a warehouse worker". It is built from "et lager" (a warehouse) and "en arbejder" (a worker). To say what job someone has, leave out "en": "Han er lagerarbejder" (He is a warehouse worker).

sentence.da: Som **lagerarbejder** pakker han varer og kører dem ud med en truck.
sentence.en: As a warehouse worker he packs goods and drives them out with a forklift.

en lagkage.explanation: "En lagkage" means "a layer cake". It is built from "et lag" (a layer) and "en kage" (a cake). To say you bake one for a birthday, say: "Jeg bager en lagkage til din fødselsdag" (I am baking a layer cake for your birthday).

sentence.da: Vi spiser **lagkage** med fløde til fødselsdagen.
sentence.en: We eat layer cake with cream for the birthday.

en lampe.explanation: "En lampe" means "a lamp". To say you switch a lamp off, use "at slukke" (to turn off): "Jeg slukker lampen" (I turn off the lamp).

sentence.da: Jeg tænder en **lampe** i det mørke rum.
sentence.en: I turn on a lamp in the dark room.

en lampeskærm.explanation: "En lampeskærm" means "a lampshade". It is built from "en lampe" (a lamp) and "en skærm" (a shade). The word "skærm" also means a screen, as in "en computerskærm" (a computer screen).

sentence.da: Pæren er skjult bag en gul **lampeskærm**.
sentence.en: The bulb is hidden behind a yellow lampshade.

en landevej.explanation: "En landevej" means "a country road". It is built from "et land" (a country) and "en vej" (a road). To say you take the country road and not the highway, use "ad" (along): "Vi kører ad landevejen i stedet for motorvejen" (We take the country road instead of the highway).

sentence.da: Vi kører langsomt på en smal **landevej**.
sentence.en: We drive slowly on a narrow country road.

en landing.explanation: "En landing" means "a landing". It comes from the verb "at lande" (to land). To say a landing was gentle, add "blød" (soft): "Det var en blød landing" (It was a soft landing).

sentence.da: Flyet havde en rolig **landing** i Kastrup.
sentence.en: The plane had a smooth landing in Kastrup.

en landingsbane.explanation: "En landingsbane" means "a runway". It is built from "en landing" (a landing) and "en bane" (a track). The word "bane" also means a court, as in "en tennisbane" (a tennis court).

sentence.da: Flyet lander på en lang **landingsbane**.
sentence.en: The plane lands on a long runway.

en landmand.explanation: "En landmand" means "a farmer". It is built from "et land" (a country) and "en mand" (a man). To say what job someone has, leave out "en": "Han er landmand" (He is a farmer).

sentence.da: En **landmand** har køer og arbejder på marken.
sentence.en: A farmer has cows and works in the field.

en landsby.explanation: "En landsby" means "a village". It is built from "et land" (a country) and "en by" (a town). To say where you live, use "i" (in): "Jeg bor i en lille landsby" (I live in a small village).

sentence.da: Der bor kun hundrede mennesker i vores **landsby**.
sentence.en: Only a hundred people live in our village.

en landskamp.explanation: "En landskamp" means "an international match". It is built from "et land" (a country) and "en kamp" (a match). To name the other country, add "mod" (against): "Landskampen mod Norge er i morgen" (The international match against Norway is tomorrow).

sentence.da: Danmark spiller **landskamp** mod Sverige i aften.
sentence.en: Denmark plays an international match against Sweden tonight.

en larve.explanation: "En larve" means "a caterpillar or larva". To say what a caterpillar eats, say: "Larven spiser bladene" (The caterpillar eats the leaves).

sentence.da: En **larve** bliver til en sommerfugl, når den er færdig med at vokse.
sentence.en: A caterpillar turns into a butterfly when it has finished growing.

en laser.explanation: "En laser" means "a laser". To say you are going to have a medical treatment with one, use "laserbehandling" (laser treatment): "Jeg skal have laserbehandling" (I am going to have laser treatment).

sentence.da: Lægen bruger en **laser** til at operere øjnene.
sentence.en: The doctor uses a laser to operate on the eyes.

en last.explanation: "En last" means "a cargo or vice". To say the goods that a ship carries, use the meaning "cargo": "Kranen løfter lasten af skibet" (The crane lifts the cargo off the ship). To say a bad habit, use the meaning "vice": "Grådighed er en last" (Greed is a vice). The opposite of a vice is "en dyd" (a virtue).

sentence.da: Skibet sejler med en tung **last** af korn.
sentence.en: The ship sails with a heavy cargo of grain.

en lastbil.explanation: "En lastbil" means "a truck". It is built from "en last" (a load) and "en bil" (a car). The word "bil" also ends other vehicle words, such as "en brandbil" (a fire engine).

sentence.da: En **lastbil** kører med varer til butikkerne.
sentence.en: A truck carries goods to the stores.

en lastbilchauffør.explanation: "En lastbilchauffør" means "a truck driver". It is built from "en lastbil" (a truck) and "en chauffør" (a driver). The spelling "ch" is said like English "sh", so "chauffør" sounds like "sjofør".

sentence.da: Min far er **lastbilchauffør** og kører meget.
sentence.en: My father is a truck driver and drives a lot.

en latter.explanation: "En latter" means "laughter". To say there was a lot of laughter, use "meget" (a lot of): "Der var meget latter" (There was a lot of laughter).

sentence.da: Fra legepladsen kunne vi høre børnenes **latter**.
sentence.en: From the playground we could hear the children's laughter.

en ledelse.explanation: "En ledelse" means "a management or leadership". It comes from the verb "at lede" (to lead). To say the people who run a company, use it for that group: "Ledelsen har besluttet det" (The management has decided that). To say the act of leading, use it for the skill: "God ledelse er vigtig" (Good leadership is important).

sentence.da: Firmaets **ledelse** bestemmer, hvordan pengene skal bruges.
sentence.en: The company's management decides how the money is to be used.

en leder.explanation: "En leder" means "a leader". The word "leder" also ends job titles, such as "en teamleder" (a team leader). For example, "Min teamleder hedder Maja" (My team leader is called Maja).

sentence.da: Vores **leder** fordeler arbejdet mellem os.
sentence.en: Our manager divides the work among us.

en ledning.explanation: "En ledning" means "a cord or cable". To say a cord is too short, say: "Ledningen er for kort" (The cord is too short). A different meaning is a pipe, as in "en vandledning" (a water pipe).

sentence.da: Telefonen får strøm gennem en **ledning**.
sentence.en: The phone gets power through a cord.

en ledsager.explanation: "En ledsager" means "a companion". It comes from the verb "at ledsage" (to accompany). To say who went along on a trip, say: "Hun var hans ledsager på rejsen" (She was his companion on the trip).

sentence.da: Du må gerne tage en **ledsager** med til festen.
sentence.en: You are welcome to bring a companion to the party.

en leg.explanation: "En leg" means "a game or play". To ask to join in, say: "Må jeg være med i legen?" (May I join the game?) Do not mix it up with "et spil" (a game), which is for a board game or sports game: "Vi spiller et spil" (We play a game).

sentence.da: Børnene har fundet på en ny **leg**.
sentence.en: The children have invented a new game.

en legende.explanation: "En legende" means "a legend". To say someone is a famous figure in their field, say: "Han er en legende i dansk fodbold" (He is a legend in Danish football). Do not mix it up with "legende" in "legende børn" (playing children), which comes from "at lege" (to play).

sentence.da: Der findes en gammel **legende** om en drage i søen.
sentence.en: There is an old legend about a dragon in the lake.

en legeplads.explanation: "En legeplads" means "a playground". It is built from "at lege" (to play) and "en plads" (a place). To say where the children are, use "på" (at): "Børnene er på legepladsen" (The children are at the playground).

sentence.da: Børnene løber rundt og leger på en **legeplads**.
sentence.en: The children run around and play on a playground.

en legetøjsbutik.explanation: "En legetøjsbutik" means "a toy store". It is built from "legetøj" (toys, without an article) and "en butik" (a store). To say where you buy a gift for a child, say: "Jeg køber en gave i legetøjsbutikken" (I buy a gift in the toy store).

sentence.da: Børnene elsker at kigge på dukker i en **legetøjsbutik**.
sentence.en: The children love looking at dolls in a toy store.

en lejebolig.explanation: "En lejebolig" means "a rental home". It is built from "at leje" (to rent) and "en bolig" (a home). To say you want to find one, say: "Jeg leder efter en lejebolig" (I am looking for a rental home).

sentence.da: Vi bor i en **lejebolig**, så vi betaler husleje hver måned.
sentence.en: We live in a rental home, so we pay rent every month.

en lejekontrakt.explanation: "En lejekontrakt" means "a lease". It is built from "at leje" (to rent) and "en kontrakt" (a contract). The word "kontrakt" also appears in "en arbejdskontrakt" (a work contract).

sentence.da: Din husleje står i en **lejekontrakt**.
sentence.en: Your rent is written in a lease.

en lejer.explanation: "En lejer" means "a tenant". It comes from the verb "at leje" (to rent). The other side is "en udlejer" (a landlord), the person who rents out a home. For example, "Vores udlejer er flink" (Our landlord is nice).

sentence.da: Jeg er **lejer** og ejer ikke lejligheden.
sentence.en: I am a tenant and do not own the apartment.

en lejlighed.explanation: "En lejlighed" means "an apartment". To say you rent one, say: "Vi lejer en lejlighed i København" (We are renting an apartment in Copenhagen). A different meaning is a chance or occasion. For example, "Jeg ringer til dig ved lejlighed" (I will call you when I get the chance).

sentence.da: Vi bor på anden sal i en **lejlighed**.
sentence.en: We live on the second floor in an apartment.

en lejr.explanation: "En lejr" means "a camp". To say a class goes to camp, say: "Klassen tager på lejr" (The class goes to camp). To say people set up a camp, use "at slå lejr" (to pitch camp): "De slog lejr ved søen" (They pitched camp by the lake).

sentence.da: Børnene sover i telte i vores **lejr**.
sentence.en: The kids sleep in tents in our camp.

en lejrskole.explanation: "En lejrskole" means "a school camp trip". It is built from "en lejr" (a camp) and "en skole" (a school). To say a class goes on one, leave out "en": "Vi tager på lejrskole" (We are going on a school camp trip).

sentence.da: Vores klasse skal på **lejrskole** til Bornholm i næste uge.
sentence.en: Our class is going on a school camp trip to Bornholm next week.

en lektion.explanation: "En lektion" means "a lesson". To say which subject, add "i" (in): "Vi har en lektion i engelsk" (We have a lesson in English). Do not mix it up with "lektier" (homework). For example, "Jeg laver lektier" (I do homework).

sentence.da: Den næste **lektion** begynder om fem minutter.
sentence.en: The next lesson begins in five minutes.

en leopard.explanation: "En leopard" means "a leopard". To say what its coat looks like, use "pletter" (spots): "En leopard har pletter" (A leopard has spots).

sentence.da: En **leopard** klatrer op i træet og sover.
sentence.en: A leopard climbs up the tree and sleeps.

en letbane.explanation: "En letbane" means "a light rail". It is built from "let" (light) and "en bane" (a track).

sentence.da: Der kører en **letbane** gennem Aarhus.
sentence.en: A light rail runs through Aarhus.

en lever.explanation: "En lever" means "a liver". In Denmark, "leverpostej" (liver pate) is a common spread on bread. Do not mix it up with "at leve" (to live). For example, "Jeg lever" (I live).

sentence.da: Din **lever** renser blodet og hjælper kroppen med at fordøje maden.
sentence.en: Your liver cleans the blood and helps the body digest food.

en leverandør.explanation: "En leverandør" means "a supplier". It comes from the verb "at levere" (to deliver). To say what a supplier supplies, add "af" (of): "Vi har en ny leverandør af kaffe" (We have a new supplier of coffee).

sentence.da: Vores **leverandør** sender friske grøntsager til restauranten hver morgen.
sentence.en: Our supplier sends fresh vegetables to the restaurant every morning.

en levering.explanation: "En levering" means "a delivery". It comes from the verb "at levere" (to deliver). To say when a delivery arrives, say: "Leveringen kommer i morgen" (The delivery arrives tomorrow).

sentence.da: Vi venter på en **levering** fra butikken.
sentence.en: We are waiting for a delivery from the store.

en leveringstid.explanation: "En leveringstid" means "a delivery time". It is built from "en levering" (a delivery) and "en tid" (a time). To ask how long you will wait, say: "Hvad er leveringstiden?" (What is the delivery time?) Do not mix it up with "en leveringsdato" (a delivery date), which is one fixed day: "Leveringsdatoen er den fjerde" (The delivery date is the fourth).

sentence.da: En lang **leveringstid** betyder, at pakken kommer sent.
sentence.en: A long delivery time means the package arrives late.

en lidelse.explanation: "En lidelse" means "a suffering or a disorder". It comes from the verb "at lide" (to suffer). To say people went through a great deal of pain, use the meaning "suffering": "Der var megen lidelse i krigen" (There was much suffering in the war).

sentence.da: Astma er en kronisk **lidelse** i lungerne.
sentence.en: Asthma is a chronic disorder of the lungs.

en lift.explanation: "En lift" means "a ride", as in being driven in someone's car. To ask for one, say: "Kan jeg få en lift?" (Can I get a ride?) To offer one, say: "Jeg giver dig en lift" (I will give you a ride).

forms.en: I will give you a ride

sentence.da: Min nabo gav mig en **lift** i sin bil.
sentence.en: My neighbor gave me a ride in his car.

en liga.explanation: "En liga" means "a league". In Denmark, the top soccer league is called "Superligaen" (the Super League). To say a team is in the league, use "i" (in): "Holdet spiller i ligaen" (The team plays in the league).

sentence.da: Alle holdene i en **liga** spiller mod hinanden hele sæsonen.
sentence.en: All the teams in a league play against each other all season.

en ligevægt.explanation: "En ligevægt" means "an equilibrium". It is built from "lige" (equal) and "en vægt" (a weight). To say someone loses their balance, say: "Han mistede ligevægten" (He lost his balance).

sentence.da: Priserne finder en **ligevægt**, når udbud og efterspørgsel er lige store.
sentence.en: Prices find an equilibrium when supply and demand are equal.

en lighed.explanation: "En lighed" means "a similarity". A very common phrase is "ligheder og forskelle" (similarities and differences). For example, "Vi ser på ligheder og forskelle" (We look at similarities and differences). A different meaning is equality. For another example, "lighed for loven" (equality before the law).

sentence.da: Der er stor **lighed** mellem de to brødre.
sentence.en: There is a strong similarity between the two brothers.

en lighter.explanation: "En lighter" means "a lighter". To ask someone for one, say: "Har du en lighter?" (Do you have a lighter?)

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke tænde bålet uden min **lighter**.
sentence.en: I can't light the fire without my lighter.

en ligning.explanation: "En ligning" means "an equation". To say you work one out, use "at løse" (to solve): "Jeg løser en ligning" (I solve an equation).

sentence.da: I en **ligning** er der altid et lighedstegn.
sentence.en: In an equation there is always an equals sign.

en lillebror.explanation: "En lillebror" means "a little brother". It is built from "lille" (little) and "en bror" (a brother). He stays your "lillebror" when he is grown up. To ask about him, say: "Hvad hedder din lillebror?" (What is your little brother called?)

sentence.da: Min **lillebror** er fem år.
sentence.en: My little brother is five years old.

en lillesøster.explanation: "En lillesøster" means "a little sister". It is built from "lille" (little) and "en søster" (a sister). She stays your "lillesøster" when she is grown up. To ask about her, say: "Hvad hedder din lillesøster?" (What is your little sister called?)

sentence.da: Min **lillesøster** er tre år.
sentence.en: My little sister is three years old.

en lime.explanation: "En lime" means "a lime". To ask for lime in a drink, say: "Vand med lime, tak" (Water with lime, please).

sentence.da: Jeg presser en **lime** over fisken.
sentence.en: I squeeze a lime over the fish.

en lineal.explanation: "En lineal" means "a ruler", as in the measuring tool. To say the other meaning, a person who rules a country, use "en hersker" (a sovereign): "Kongen var en mægtig hersker" (The king was a powerful ruler).

sentence.da: Jeg måler papiret med en **lineal**.
sentence.en: I measure the paper with a ruler.

en linje.explanation: "En linje" means "a line". To say a bus or train route, use it with a number: "Tag linje 5" (Take line 5). For people waiting in a line, use "en kø" (a queue): "Der er en lang kø" (There is a long queue).

sentence.da: Tegn en lige **linje** på papiret.
sentence.en: Draw a straight line on the paper.

en liste.explanation: "En liste" means "a list". A common word built with it is "en gæsteliste" (a guest list). To say someone is on that list, say: "Du står på gæstelisten" (You are on the guest list).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver mælk og brød på en **liste**.
sentence.en: I write milk and bread on a list.

en liter.explanation: "En liter" means "a liter". To name the liquid you measure, put it right after: "en liter vand" (a liter of water).

sentence.da: Jeg køber to **liter** mælk.
sentence.en: I am buying two liters of milk.

en litteraturliste.explanation: "En litteraturliste" means "a bibliography". It is built from "en litteratur" (literature) and "en liste" (a list).

sentence.da: Sidst i opgaven skal der være en **litteraturliste** med alle bøgerne.
sentence.en: At the end of the paper there must be a bibliography with all the books.

en livredder.explanation: "En livredder" means "a lifeguard". It is built from "et liv" (a life) and "en redder" (a rescuer). To warn that something is deadly, use "liv" in another word: "Det er livsfarligt" (It is life-threatening).

sentence.da: En **livredder** passer på børnene ved vandet.
sentence.en: A lifeguard watches the children by the water.

en livret.explanation: "En livret" means "a favorite dish". It is built from "et liv" (a life) and "en ret" (a dish). To say how many dishes a dinner has, use "ret" in the plural: "en middag med tre retter" (a dinner with three dishes).

sentence.da: Min **livret** er lasagne, og jeg elsker den.
sentence.en: My favorite dish is lasagna, and I love it.

en livsstil.explanation: "En livsstil" means "a lifestyle". It is built from "et liv" (a life) and "en stil" (a style). To say something does not suit your taste, use the word "stil" alone: "Det er ikke min stil" (That is not my style).

sentence.da: Hun har en meget sund **livsstil**.
sentence.en: She has a very healthy lifestyle.

en livstid.explanation: "En livstid" means "a lifetime". To say a judge sent someone to prison for life, use the same word: "Han fik livstid" (He got a life sentence).

sentence.da: Det sker kun én gang i en **livstid**.
sentence.en: It only happens once in a lifetime.

en lobby.explanation: "En lobby" means "a lobby". English speakers would write "lobbies" for more than one, but the Danish plural is "lobbyer": "to lobbyer" (two lobbies).

sentence.da: Vi venter i hotellets **lobby**.
sentence.en: We are waiting in the hotel's lobby.

en lobbyist.explanation: "En lobbyist" means "a lobbyist". The work such a person does is called "lobbyisme" (lobbying).

sentence.da: Firmaet har hyret en **lobbyist** til at påvirke ministeren.
sentence.en: The company has hired a lobbyist to influence the minister.

en loftslampe.explanation: "En loftslampe" means "a ceiling light". It is built from "et loft" (a ceiling) and "en lampe" (a lamp). To say where old things are stored, use "loft" for the attic: "Vi har gamle ting på loftet" (We have old things in the attic).

sentence.da: En **loftslampe** hænger i loftet over bordet.
sentence.en: A ceiling light hangs from the ceiling over the table.

en lokalavis.explanation: "En lokalavis" means "a local newspaper". It is built from "lokal" (local) and "en avis" (a newspaper).

sentence.da: Vores **lokalavis** skriver om skolen, markedet og byrådet.
sentence.en: Our local newspaper writes about the school, the market and the town council.

en lokalbefolkning.explanation: "En lokalbefolkning" means "a local population". It is built from "lokal" (local) and "en befolkning" (a population).

sentence.da: Kun en lille **lokalbefolkning** bor på øen hele året.
sentence.en: Only a small local population lives on the island all year.

en lokomotivfører.explanation: "En lokomotivfører" means "a train driver". It is built from "et lokomotiv" (a locomotive) and "en fører" (a driver).

sentence.da: En **lokomotivfører** sidder forrest og kører toget.
sentence.en: A train driver sits at the front and drives the train.

en lomme.explanation: "En lomme" means "a pocket". To say where you keep something, say: "Mine nøgler er i lommen" (My keys are in my pocket).

sentence.da: Min jakke har en **lomme** til telefonen.
sentence.en: My jacket has a pocket for the phone.

en lommelygte.explanation: "En lommelygte" means "a flashlight". It is built from "en lomme" (a pocket) and "en lygte" (a light). The part "lygte" is also in "en baglygte" (a taillight) and "en forlygte" (a headlight).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger en **lommelygte**, fordi det er mørkt.
sentence.en: I use a flashlight because it is dark.

en lommeregner.explanation: "En lommeregner" means "a calculator". It is built from "en lomme" (a pocket) and "at regne" (to calculate). The part "lomme" is also in "lommepenge" (pocket money) and "en lommekniv" (a pocket knife).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger en **lommeregner** til matematik.
sentence.en: I use a calculator for math.

en loppe.explanation: "En loppe" means "a flea". The start of the word is in "et loppemarked" (a flea market). To say you are going to one, say: "Vi går på loppemarked i morgen" (We are going to a flea market tomorrow).

sentence.da: En **loppe** kan hoppe langt og bor i hundens pels.
sentence.en: A flea can jump far and lives in the dog's fur.

en lov.explanation: "En lov" means "a law". To say something breaks the law, say: "Det er imod loven" (It is against the law). When you say something is allowed, "lov" also has that meaning: "Det er ikke lov at parkere her" (It is not allowed to park here).

sentence.da: Der er en ny **lov** om cykelhjelme.
sentence.en: There is a new law about bicycle helmets.

en lufthavn.explanation: "En lufthavn" means "an airport". It is built from "luft" (air) and "en havn" (a harbor). To say where a boat is, use the word "havn" alone: "Båden ligger i havnen" (The boat is in the harbor).

sentence.da: Flyene lander og letter i en stor **lufthavn**.
sentence.en: The planes land and take off at a big airport.

en lugt.explanation: "En lugt" means "a smell". To describe a pleasant smell, use "en duft" (a scent): "Der er en duft af kaffe" (There is a scent of coffee).

sentence.da: Der er en dejlig **lugt** i køkkenet.
sentence.en: There is a lovely smell in the kitchen.

en lukkedag.explanation: "En lukkedag" means "a closing day". It is built from "at lukke" (to close) and "en dag" (a day). To ask when a shop shuts for the day, use "en lukketid" (a closing time): "Hvad er lukketiden?" (What is the closing time?)

sentence.da: Børnehaven har en **lukkedag** mellem jul og nytår.
sentence.en: The daycare has a closing day between Christmas and New Year.

en lukketid.explanation: "En lukketid" means "a closing time". It is built from "at lukke" (to close) and "en tid" (a time). To say a place is shut for a whole day, use "en lukkedag" (a closing day): "Vi har lukkedag i morgen" (We are closed all day tomorrow).

sentence.da: Ved **lukketid** går alle gæsterne hjem fra baren.
sentence.en: At closing time all the guests go home from the bar.

en lunge.explanation: "En lunge" means "a lung". To name the illness, use "lungebetændelse" (pneumonia), built from "lunge" and "en betændelse" (an inflammation): "Hun har lungebetændelse" (She has pneumonia).

sentence.da: Hjertet sidder mellem den højre og venstre **lunge**.
sentence.en: The heart sits between the right and left lung.

en lup.explanation: "En lup" means "a magnifying glass". To ask to borrow one, say: "Må jeg låne din lup?" (May I borrow your magnifying glass?)

sentence.da: Teksten er lille, så jeg bruger en **lup**.
sentence.en: The text is small, so I use a magnifying glass.

en lur.explanation: "En lur" means "a nap". When you talk about a phone receiver, "lur" has that second meaning: "Han tog luren" (He picked up the receiver).

sentence.da: Efter frokost lægger han sig og tager en **lur**.
sentence.en: After lunch he lies down and takes a nap.

en lus.explanation: "En lus" means "a louse". The plural has no ending, so it looks the same as the singular. For example, "to lus" (two lice).

sentence.da: Mange børn får **lus** i håret, når de leger tæt sammen.
sentence.en: Many children get lice in their hair when they play close together.

en lyd.explanation: "En lyd" means "a sound". To tell someone to make a device louder, use the second meaning, the volume: "Skru op for lyden" (Turn up the volume).

sentence.da: Vi hørte en høj **lyd** i natten.
sentence.en: We heard a loud sound in the night.

en lydbog.explanation: "En lydbog" means "an audiobook". It is built from "en lyd" (a sound) and "en bog" (a book). English speakers would guess "lydbøger" wrongly as "lydbogs": the plural changes "o" to "ø", so two audiobooks are "to lydbøger".

sentence.da: Jeg lytter til en **lydbog**, når jeg går tur.
sentence.en: I listen to an audiobook when I go for a walk.

en lygte.explanation: "En lygte" means "a light". To name a light for a bike, add "cykel" in front: "en cykellygte" (a bike light). To talk about a lamp in a room, use "en lampe" (a lamp): "Lampen står på bordet" (The lamp is on the table).

forms.en: a light, a lamp (on a bike or in the street)

sentence.da: Når det bliver mørkt, tænder jeg min **lygte**.
sentence.en: When it gets dark, I turn on my light.

en lynlås.explanation: "En lynlås" means "a zipper". To say you close the zipper, say: "Jeg lukker lynlåsen" (I close the zipper).

sentence.da: Jakken har en **lynlås** foran, ikke knapper.
sentence.en: The jacket has a zipper in front, not buttons.

en lysestage.explanation: "En lysestage" means "a candlestick". The first part, "lys", means "a candle" here. To say you light a candle, say: "Jeg tænder et lys" (I light a candle).

sentence.da: Du sætter lyset i en **lysestage** og tænder det.
sentence.en: You put the candle in a candlestick and light it.

en lyskontakt.explanation: "En lyskontakt" means "a light switch". It is built from "lys" (light) and "en kontakt" (a switch). To ask someone to turn the light on, say: "Tænd lyset" (Turn on the light).

sentence.da: Der er en **lyskontakt** ved siden af døren.
sentence.en: There is a light switch next to the door.

en lysning.explanation: "En lysning" means "a clearing". It comes from "lys" (light). To say where a clearing is, add "i skoven" (in the forest): "en lysning i skoven" (a clearing in the forest).

sentence.da: Mellem træerne er der en åben **lysning** med masser af sol.
sentence.en: Between the trees there is an open clearing with lots of sun.

en lyspære.explanation: "En lyspære" means "a lightbulb". It is built from "lys" (light) and "en pære" (a pear). To say you replace a burned-out bulb, say: "Jeg skifter pæren" (I change the bulb).

sentence.da: Jeg skal købe en ny **lyspære** til lampen.
sentence.en: I have to buy a new lightbulb for the lamp.

en lytteøvelse.explanation: "En lytteøvelse" means "a listening exercise". It is built from "at lytte" (to listen) and "en øvelse" (an exercise). "At lytte" means to listen on purpose. For example, "Jeg lytter til musik" (I listen to music). "At høre" means to hear without trying. For another example, "Jeg hører en lyd" (I hear a sound).

sentence.da: I en **lytteøvelse** hører du en samtale og svarer på spørgsmål.
sentence.en: In a listening exercise you hear a conversation and answer questions.

en låge.explanation: "En låge" means "a gate". To talk about a large gate for cars, use "en port" (a large gate): "Bilen holder foran porten" (The car stops in front of the gate).

sentence.da: Der er en lille **låge** ind til haven.
sentence.en: There is a small gate into the garden.

en lås.explanation: "En lås" means "a lock". The matching verb is "at låse" (to lock). For example, "Husk at låse døren" (Remember to lock the door).

sentence.da: Jeg sætter en **lås** på min cykel.
sentence.en: I put a lock on my bike.

en læbe.explanation: "En læbe" means "a lip". To name the makeup for your lips, use "en læbestift" (a lipstick): "Hun køber en læbestift" (She buys a lipstick).

sentence.da: Munden har en øvre og en nedre **læbe**.
sentence.en: The mouth has an upper and a lower lip.

en læbestift.explanation: "En læbestift" means "a lipstick". It starts with "en læbe" (a lip), which is also in "en læbepomade" (a lip balm).

sentence.da: Hun tager rød **læbestift** på.
sentence.en: She puts on red lipstick.

en læg.explanation: "En læg" means "a calf (of the leg)". Do not mix it up with "en læge" (a doctor), which has one more letter. For example, "Jeg ringer til lægen" (I call the doctor).

sentence.da: Jeg fik krampe i min **læg** under løbeturen.
sentence.en: I got a cramp in my calf during the run.

en læge.explanation: "En læge" means "a doctor". To say you are going to see your doctor, say: "Jeg går til lægen" (I am going to the doctor).

sentence.da: Jeg er syg og ringer til en **læge**.
sentence.en: I am sick and call a doctor.

en lægevagt.explanation: "En lægevagt" means "an after-hours medical service". It is built from "en læge" (a doctor) and "en vagt" (a duty).

sentence.da: Der findes en **lægevagt**, som har åbent hele natten.
sentence.en: There is an after-hours medical service that is open all night.

en lænestol.explanation: "En lænestol" means "an armchair". It is built from "at læne sig" (to lean back) and "en stol" (a chair).

sentence.da: Han sidder i en **lænestol** og læser avis.
sentence.en: He sits in an armchair and reads the newspaper.

en længde.explanation: "En længde" means "a length". To say how many times you swim from one end of a pool to the other, use the same word: "Jeg svømmer ti længder" (I swim ten lengths).

sentence.da: Bordets **længde** er to meter.
sentence.en: The table's length is two meters.

en lænke.explanation: "En lænke" means "a chain". To say a prisoner was chained, say: "Fangen blev lagt i lænker" (The prisoner was put in chains). For an ordinary chain, such as on a bike, use "en kæde" (a chain): "Cyklen har en rusten kæde" (The bike has a rusty chain).

sentence.da: Fangen havde en tung **lænke** om anklen.
sentence.en: The prisoner had a heavy chain around his ankle.

en lærebog.explanation: "En lærebog" means "a textbook". It is built from "at lære" (to learn) and "en bog" (a book). "At lære" also means "to teach". For example, "Hun lærer mig dansk" (She teaches me Danish).

sentence.da: Min **lærebog** i dansk er meget tyk.
sentence.en: My Danish textbook is very thick.

en lærer.explanation: "En lærer" means "a teacher", for a man or a woman. To say someone's job, leave out "en": "Hun er lærer" (She is a teacher).

sentence.da: Vores **lærer** underviser os i dansk i skolen.
sentence.en: Our teacher teaches us Danish at school.

en lærestreg.explanation: "En lærestreg" means "a hard lesson". To talk about a lesson in school, use "en lektion" (a lesson): "Lektionen starter klokken ni" (The lesson starts at nine o'clock).

sentence.da: Det blev en dyr **lærestreg**, da jeg mistede min telefon.
sentence.en: It became an expensive lesson when I lost my phone.

en lærling.explanation: "En lærling" means "an apprentice". In Denmark, an apprentice learns a trade by working at a company and also by attending trade school.

sentence.da: I tre år er han **lærling** hos en tømrer.
sentence.en: For three years he is an apprentice with a carpenter.

en læser.explanation: "En læser" means "a reader". The same word is also the verb form of "at læse" (to read). For example, "Hun læser en bog" (She reads a book).

sentence.da: Hun er en flittig **læser** og låner mange bøger.
sentence.en: She is a diligent reader and borrows many books.

en læsesal.explanation: "En læsesal" means "a reading room". It is built from "at læse" (to read) and "en sal" (a hall).

sentence.da: Det er forbudt at snakke højt på en **læsesal**.
sentence.en: It is forbidden to talk loudly in a reading room.

en læsning.explanation: "En læsning" means "a reading". To say you give your own understanding of a text, use it with "en": "en kritisk læsning af romanen" (a critical reading of the novel). To talk about reading as a skill or school subject, leave out "en": "Vi har læsning i anden time" (We have reading in second period).

sentence.da: Hendes **læsning** af digtet var meget anderledes end min.
sentence.en: Her reading of the poem was very different from mine.

en løbesko.explanation: "En løbesko" means "a running shoe". It is built from "at løbe" (to run) and "en sko" (a shoe). The plural has no ending. For example, "to løbesko" (two running shoes). The start "løbe-" means "for running" in other words too. For another example, "et løbebånd" (a treadmill).

sentence.da: Jeg har nye **løbesko**, så jeg løber en tur.
sentence.en: I have new running shoes, so I am going for a run.

en løbetur.explanation: "En løbetur" means "a run". It is built from "at løbe" (to run) and "en tur" (a trip). To say it is someone's turn, "tur" has another meaning: "Det er din tur" (It is your turn).

sentence.da: Jeg tager en **løbetur** i parken hver morgen.
sentence.en: I go for a run in the park every morning.

en løgn.explanation: "En løgn" means "a lie". To say someone told a lie, use "at fortælle" (to tell) with it: "Han fortalte en løgn" (He told a lie).

sentence.da: Det er en **løgn**, og det ved du godt.
sentence.en: That is a lie, and you know it.

en løgner.explanation: "En løgner" means "a liar". It is a blunt word, and calling someone "en løgner" is a strong accusation. To say in a milder way that a statement is wrong, say: "Det passer ikke" (That is not true).

sentence.da: Han er en **løgner** og fortæller aldrig sandheden.
sentence.en: He is a liar and never tells the truth.

en løjtnant.explanation: "En løjtnant" means "a lieutenant". English speakers would spell it like the English word, but the Danish spelling is "løjtnant", with "ø" and "j" at the start.

sentence.da: En **løjtnant** er officer og leder en lille gruppe soldater.
sentence.en: A lieutenant is an officer and leads a small group of soldiers.

en løkke.explanation: "En løkke" means "a loop". To talk about computer code that repeats the same steps, use the same word: "en løkke i programmet" (a loop in the program).

sentence.da: Du kan lave en **løkke** i rebet og hænge den på krogen.
sentence.en: You can make a loop in the rope and hang it on the hook.

en løn.explanation: "En løn" means "a salary". To talk about pay for each hour, use "timeløn" (hourly pay).

sentence.da: Jeg får min **løn** den første i måneden.
sentence.en: I get my salary on the first of the month.

en lønforhøjelse.explanation: "En lønforhøjelse" means "a raise". It is built from "løn" (pay) and "en forhøjelse" (an increase). To say what you would like from your boss, say: "Jeg vil gerne have en lønforhøjelse" (I would like a raise).

sentence.da: Efter to gode år fik hun endelig en **lønforhøjelse**.
sentence.en: After two good years she finally got a raise.

en lønseddel.explanation: "En lønseddel" means "a paystub". The part "seddel" (a slip of paper) is also in "en pengeseddel" (a banknote). Note the spelling of "the paystub". For example, "lønsedlen" has one "d" less than "lønseddel".

sentence.da: På din **lønseddel** står både din løn og din skat.
sentence.en: Your paystub shows both your pay and your tax.

en løsning.explanation: "En løsning" means "a solution". It comes from "at løse" (to solve). To say you find a way out of a problem, say: "Vi finder en løsning" (We find a solution).

sentence.da: Vi har et problem og leder efter en **løsning**.
sentence.en: We have a problem and are looking for a solution.

en løve.explanation: "En løve" means "a lion". To say a female lion, use "en løvinde" (a lioness): "Løvinden ligger i skyggen" (The lioness lies in the shade). The word is also the first part of "en løvetand" (a dandelion), literally "lion tooth".

sentence.da: En **løve** brøler højt.
sentence.en: A lion roars loudly.

et laboratorium.explanation: "Et laboratorium" means "a laboratory". The plural drops "um" and ends in "-er". For example, "to laboratorier" (two laboratories).

sentence.da: Hun arbejder i et **laboratorium** og undersøger blodprøver.
sentence.en: She works in a laboratory and examines blood samples.

et lag.explanation: "Et lag" means "a layer". The word is also the start of "en lagkage" (a layer cake). For example, "Vi spiser lagkage" (We eat layer cake).

sentence.da: Der ligger et tykt **lag** sne på taget.
sentence.en: There is a thick layer of snow on the roof.

et lagen.explanation: "Et lagen" means "a sheet", as in a bed sheet. To ask for a sheet of paper, use "et ark" (a sheet of paper): "Giv mig et ark papir" (Give me a sheet of paper).

sentence.da: Jeg skal skifte **lagen** på sengen i dag.
sentence.en: I have to change the sheet on the bed today.

et lager.explanation: "Et lager" means "a warehouse or stock". To ask whether a shop has an item, say: "Er den på lager?" (Is it in stock?)

sentence.da: Alle varerne står i et stort **lager** uden for byen.
sentence.en: All the goods are in a big warehouse outside the city.

et lam.explanation: "Et lam" means "a lamb". To talk about lamb as meat, leave out "et": "Jeg elsker lam" (I love lamb).

sentence.da: Et **lam** er et ungt får.
sentence.en: A lamb is a young sheep.

et land.explanation: "Et land" means "a country". The same word also means "countryside" in "på landet" (in the countryside). To say where you live, say: "Jeg bor på landet" (I live in the countryside).

sentence.da: Danmark er et lille **land**.
sentence.en: Denmark is a small country.

et landbrug.explanation: "Et landbrug" means "agriculture or a farm". To talk about farming as an industry, say: "Der er meget landbrug i Danmark" (There is a lot of agriculture in Denmark). To talk about the farmhouse and its yard, use "en gård" (a farm): "Vi bor på en gård" (We live on a farm).

sentence.da: Min onkel har et **landbrug** med køer og grise.
sentence.en: My uncle has a farm with cows and pigs.

et landkort.explanation: "Et landkort" means "a map". It is built from "et land" (a country) and "et kort" (a map or a card). The plural has no ending. For example, "to landkort" (two maps).

sentence.da: På et **landkort** kan man se alle lande.
sentence.en: On a map you can see all the countries.

et landshold.explanation: "Et landshold" means "a national team". It is built from "et land" (a country) and "et hold" (a team). To say a player is on that team, say: "Han spiller på landsholdet" (He plays on the national team).

sentence.da: Vores **landshold** vandt kampen i går.
sentence.en: Our national team won the match yesterday.

et landskab.explanation: "Et landskab" means "a landscape". To talk about what you see from one spot, use "en udsigt" (a view): "Der er en flot udsigt fra bjerget" (There is a nice view from the mountain).

sentence.da: Marker, skove og søer er en del af et **landskab**.
sentence.en: Fields, forests and lakes are part of a landscape.

et lavtryk.explanation: "Et lavtryk" means "a low-pressure system". It is built from "lav" (low) and "et tryk" (pressure). The opposite is "et højtryk" (a high-pressure system). For example, "Et højtryk ligger over Danmark" (A high-pressure system lies over Denmark).

sentence.da: Et **lavtryk** fra Atlanterhavet giver regn og blæst i weekenden.
sentence.en: A low-pressure system from the Atlantic brings rain and wind this weekend.

et led.explanation: "Et led" means "a joint". To say something is one step in a series, use "et led i kæden" (a link in the chain).

sentence.da: Fingeren har tre **led**, så du kan bøje den.
sentence.en: The finger has three joints, so you can bend it.

et leksikon.explanation: "Et leksikon" means "an encyclopedia". To look up the meaning of a word instead, use "en ordbog" (a dictionary): "Jeg slår ordet op i en ordbog" (I look the word up in a dictionary).

sentence.da: I et **leksikon** kan du læse om mange emner fra A til Å.
sentence.en: In an encyclopedia you can read about many topics from A to Z.

et lig.explanation: "Et lig" means "a corpse". It is a blunt word. A gentler way to speak of a dead person is "den afdøde" (the deceased person). For example, "Familien sørger over den afdøde" (The family mourns the deceased person).

sentence.da: Politiet fandt et **lig** i skoven tidligt i morges.
sentence.en: The police found a corpse in the forest early this morning.

et like.explanation: "Et like" means "a like". To say you give one on social media, say: "Jeg giver et like" (I give a like).

sentence.da: Mit billede fik et **like** fra min mor.
sentence.en: My picture got a like from my mom.

et link.explanation: "Et link" means "a link". To ask someone to send one, say: "Send mig et link" (Send me a link).

sentence.da: Klik på det **link** for at se videoen.
sentence.en: Click on that link to see the video.

et liv.explanation: "Et liv" means "a life". To talk about life in general, use the form "livet": "Livet er godt" (Life is good). To talk about one person's life, use "et liv": "at have et godt liv" (to have a good life).

sentence.da: Vi har kun ét **liv**.
sentence.en: We only have one life.

et loft.explanation: "Et loft" means "a ceiling or attic". When you talk about the top of a room, it means "ceiling": "Der er en lampe i loftet" (There is a lamp in the ceiling). When you talk about the space under the roof, it means "attic": "Vi har gamle ting på loftet" (We have old things in the attic).

sentence.da: Vi bor i en lejlighed med et højt **loft**.
sentence.en: We live in an apartment with a high ceiling.

et loftsrum.explanation: "Et loftsrum" means "an attic room". It is built from "et loft" (an attic) and "et rum" (a room).

related.en: a top floor under the roof

sentence.da: Børneværelset ligger i et lille **loftsrum** under taget.
sentence.en: The children's room is in a small attic room under the roof.

et loppemarked.explanation: "Et loppemarked" means "a flea market". It is built from "en loppe" (a flea) and "et marked" (a market). To say you go to one, say: "Vi går på loppemarked i morgen" (We are going to a flea market tomorrow).

sentence.da: Folk sælger brugte ting på et **loppemarked**.
sentence.en: People sell used things at a flea market.

et lotteri.explanation: "Et lotteri" means "a lottery". To say someone won a prize in one, say: "Han vandt i lotteriet" (He won the lottery). The plural is "lotterier". For example, "to lotterier" (two lotteries).

sentence.da: Skolen holder et **lotteri**, og alle kan vinde en præmie.
sentence.en: The school holds a lottery, and everyone can win a prize.

et lovforslag.explanation: "Et lovforslag" means "a bill". It is built from "lov" (law) and "et forslag" (a proposal). To say parliament approves one, use "at vedtage" (to pass): "Folketinget vedtager lovforslaget" (The Danish parliament passes the bill).

sentence.da: Politikerne diskuterer et nyt **lovforslag** om skat i dag.
sentence.en: The politicians are discussing a new bill about tax today.

et lykønskningskort.explanation: "Et lykønskningskort" means "a congratulations card". It is built from "en lykønskning" (a congratulation) and "et kort" (a card). To congratulate someone aloud, say: "Tillykke!" (Congratulations!)

sentence.da: Vi sendte et **lykønskningskort** til de nygifte.
sentence.en: We sent a congratulations card to the newlyweds.

et lyskryds.explanation: "Et lyskryds" means "an intersection with traffic lights". It is built from "lys" (light) and "et kryds" (a cross). For an intersection without traffic lights, use "et vejkryds" (an intersection): "Vi mødes i vejkrydset" (We meet at the intersection).

sentence.da: Drej til højre ved det næste **lyskryds**.
sentence.en: Turn right at the next intersection with traffic lights.

et lån.explanation: "Et lån" means "a loan". The verb "at låne" means both "to borrow" and "to lend". For example, "Jeg låner dig en pen" (I lend you a pen).

sentence.da: Jeg skal have et **lån**, når jeg køber huset.
sentence.en: I need a loan when I buy the house.

et lår.explanation: "Et lår" means "a thigh". To name a part of a chicken, put the animal in front: "et kyllingelår" (a chicken thigh).

sentence.da: Mit **lår** er over mit knæ.
sentence.en: My thigh is above my knee.

et læserbrev.explanation: "Et læserbrev" means "a letter to the editor". It is built from "en læser" (a reader) and "et brev" (a letter). English speakers would guess the plural wrongly: it is "læserbreve", not "læserbrever".

sentence.da: Hun skrev et **læserbrev**, fordi hun var uenig i artiklen.
sentence.en: She wrote a letter to the editor because she disagreed with the article.

et løbebånd.explanation: "Et løbebånd" means "a treadmill". It is built from "at løbe" (to run) and "et bånd" (a belt). The plural has no ending. For example, "to løbebånd" (two treadmills).

sentence.da: Når det regner, løber hun på et **løbebånd** indendørs.
sentence.en: When it rains, she runs on a treadmill indoors.

et løfte.explanation: "Et løfte" means "a promise". To say you keep a promise, use "at holde" (to hold): "Jeg holder mit løfte" (I keep my promise). To say you break one, use "at bryde" (to break): "Han brød sit løfte" (He broke his promise).

sentence.da: Et **løfte** skal man holde.
sentence.en: A promise must be kept.

et løg.explanation: "Et løg" means "an onion". The word is also part of "hvidløg" (garlic), literally "white onion".

sentence.da: Et **løg** får mig til at græde.
sentence.en: An onion makes me cry.

lad os se.explanation: "Lad os se" means "Let's see." To suggest doing something together, put "lad os" (let us) before a verb: "Lad os gå" (Let us go). To say you will check, answer a question like this: "Er der mere mælk?" "Lad os se." (Is there more milk? Let's see.)

forms.da: Lad os se, hvad klokken er.
forms.en: Let's see what time it is.

forms.da: Lad os se, om han kommer.

sentence.da: **Lad os se** i køleskabet.
sentence.en: Let's look in the fridge.

lad være.explanation: "Lad være" means "Don't!" To tell someone not to do something, add "med at" and a verb: "Lad være med at ringe" (Don't call). In the past, "lad" becomes "lod". For example, "Han lod være" (He left it alone).

forms.da: Lad være med at spise det

sentence.da: **Lad være** med at røre ved kagen!
sentence.en: Don't touch the cake!

lakrids.explanation: "Lakrids" means "licorice". To name ice cream with that flavor, add "is" (ice cream): "lakridsis" (licorice ice cream).

sentence.da: **Lakrids** er sort og lidt salt.
sentence.en: Licorice is black and a little salty.

laks.explanation: "Laks" means "salmon". To count whole fish, use "en laks" (a salmon): "Han fanger en laks" (He catches a salmon). To talk about salmon as food, leave out "en": "Jeg spiser laks" (I eat salmon).

sentence.da: **Laks** er en lyserød fisk.
sentence.en: Salmon is a pink fish.

laktosefri.explanation: "Laktosefri" means "lactose-free". It is built from "laktose" (lactose) and "fri" (free). The same ending is in "glutenfri" (gluten-free) and "sukkerfri" (sugar-free). With a word that takes "et", add "t": "et laktosefrit produkt" (a lactose-free product).

sentence.da: Han køber **laktosefri** ost, fordi han ikke tåler laktose.
sentence.en: He buys lactose-free cheese because he cannot tolerate lactose.

lammekød.explanation: "Lammekød" means "lamb", the meat. It is built from "et lam" (a lamb) and "kød" (meat).

sentence.da: **Lammekød** kommer fra unge får.
sentence.en: Lamb comes from young sheep.

lammet.explanation: "Lammet" means "paralyzed". To say someone is frozen by fear, use it too: "Hun stod lammet af skræk" (She stood paralyzed by fear). Do not mix it up with "lammet" meaning "the lamb", which is "et lam" (a lamb) with "the" added. For example, "Lammet løber" (The lamb runs).

sentence.da: Hun stod **lammet** af skræk og kunne ikke sige noget.
sentence.en: She stood paralyzed by fear and could not say anything.

lang.explanation: "Lang" means "long". To say something is far away, use the form "langt": "Det er langt væk" (It is far away).

sentence.da: Giraffen har en **lang** hals.
sentence.en: The giraffe has a long neck.

langfredag.explanation: "Langfredag" means "Good Friday". It is a day off in Denmark. The name literally means "long Friday".

sentence.da: På **langfredag** har de fleste fri fra arbejde.
sentence.en: On Good Friday most people have the day off work.

langs.explanation: "Langs" means "along". To say you walk next to a shore, put it before the place: "Vi går langs stranden" (We walk along the beach). To say the same with the word last, put it after the place: "Vi går stranden langs" (We walk along the beach).

sentence.da: Der står træer **langs** vejen.
sentence.en: There are trees along the road.

langsom.explanation: "Langsom" means "slow". To say that something happens slowly, use "langsomt" (slowly): "Tal langsomt, tak" (Speak slowly, please).

sentence.da: Skildpadden er meget **langsom**.
sentence.en: The turtle is very slow.

langt fra.explanation: "Langt fra" means "far from". To say where something is, say the place right after it: "Hun bor langt fra byen" (She lives far from the town). To say something is far away without naming a place, use "langt væk" (far away): "Hotellet er langt væk" (The hotel is far away). To answer that something is not true at all, say "Langt fra!": "Er du sulten?" "Langt fra!" (Are you hungry? Far from it!)

forms.en: The hotel is far from the town.

sentence.da: Vores hus ligger **langt fra** byen.
sentence.en: Our house is far from the town.

langt væk.explanation: "Langt væk" means "far away". To say something is far away, end the phrase with it: "Hotellet er langt væk" (The hotel is far away). To say far from a named place, use "langt fra" (far from) with the place after it: "Hun bor langt fra byen" (She lives far from the town).

sentence.da: Min familie bor **langt væk**.
sentence.en: My family lives far away.

langtrukken.explanation: "Langtrukken" means "long-winded". To say a meeting takes too long, use the form ending in "-ent": "Mødet var langtrukkent" (The meeting was long-winded).

sentence.da: Talen var **langtrukken**, og mange begyndte at gabe.
sentence.en: The speech was long-winded and many began to yawn.

langvarig.explanation: "Langvarig" means "long-lasting". It is about how long something lasts. To say rain keeps on for a long time, say: "Der var langvarigt regn" (There was long-lasting rain). To say rain is heavy, use "kraftig" (heavy): "Der var kraftigt regn" (There was heavy rain).

sentence.da: Efter en **langvarig** sygdom kom han endelig tilbage på arbejde.
sentence.en: After a long illness he finally came back to work.

larm.explanation: "Larm" means "noise". It is the noun for the verb "at larme" (to make a racket). To tell someone to stop the noise, say: "Hold op med larmen!" (Stop the noise!)

sentence.da: Der er for meget **larm** på gaden.
sentence.en: There is too much noise on the street.

larmende.explanation: "Larmende" means "noisy". It is made from the verb "at larme" (to make a racket) plus the ending "-ende", which is like English "-ing".

sentence.da: Børnene i klassen er **larmende**, når læreren går ud.
sentence.en: The children in the class are noisy when the teacher leaves.
