latin.explanation: "Latin" means "Latin". To ask the Latin word for something, use "på" (in): "Hvad hedder det på latin?" (What is it called in Latin?). To describe a word as Latin, use "latinsk" (Latin): "et latinsk ord" (a Latin word).

sentence.da: Lægerne bruger mange ord fra **latin**.
sentence.en: Doctors use many words from Latin.

latterlig.explanation: "Latterlig" means "ridiculous". It comes from "en latter" (laughter). To say someone makes a fool of themselves, use "at gøre sig latterlig" (to make oneself ridiculous): "Du gør dig latterlig" (You are making a fool of yourself).

sentence.da: Det er en **latterlig** pris for en kop kaffe.
sentence.en: That is a ridiculous price for a cup of coffee.

lav.explanation: "Lav" means "low". To say prices are low, use the plural: "Priserne er lave" (The prices are low). The same spelling is also the command form of "at lave" (to make). For example, "Lav en kop te" (Make a cup of tea).

sentence.da: Stolen er **lav**, ikke høj.
sentence.en: The chair is low, not high.

lava.explanation: "En lava" means "lava". Do not mix it up with "lav" (low), which has no "a" at the end. For example, "Stolen er lav" (The chair is low).

sentence.da: Den røde **lava** flyder ned ad bjergets side.
sentence.en: The red lava flows down the side of the mountain.

ledig.explanation: "Ledig" means "vacant". To say a job is open, use "en ledig stilling" (a job opening): "Der er en ledig stilling i butikken" (There is a job opening in the shop). To say a person has no job, use it about the person: "Han er ledig" (He is out of work).

sentence.da: Er der en **ledig** plads her?
sentence.en: Is there a free seat here?

legetøj.explanation: "Legetøj" means "toys". This word has no article, so leave out "et". For example, "Jeg har legetøj" (I have toys). When you talk about one specific kind of toy, use its name: "en bamse" (a teddy bear).

sentence.da: Barnet leger med sit **legetøj**.
sentence.en: The child plays with their toys.

leggings.explanation: "Leggings" means "leggings". The word comes from English and is spelled the same way. To say you are putting them on, use "tage på" (to put on): "Jeg tager leggings på" (I put on leggings).

sentence.da: Hun løber i sorte **leggings** hver morgen.
sentence.en: She runs in black leggings every morning.

lejlighedsvis.explanation: "Lejlighedsvis" means "occasionally". It is built from "en lejlighed" (an occasion). To say how often you play, put it after the verb: "Jeg spiller lejlighedsvis fodbold" (I play soccer occasionally).

forms.en: He occasionally works as an interpreter

sentence.da: Jeg cykler **lejlighedsvis** på arbejde, når vejret er godt.
sentence.en: I occasionally bike to work when the weather is good.

lektier.explanation: "Lektier" means "homework". To say you do your homework, use "at lave" (to do): "Jeg laver lektier" (I do my homework). To ask a pupil whether homework is due, say: "Har du lektier for?" (Do you have homework?)

sentence.da: Læreren giver os **lektier** til i morgen.
sentence.en: The teacher gives us homework for tomorrow.

ler.explanation: "Ler" means "clay". To say what children play with, say: "Børnene leger med ler" (The children play with clay). Do not mix it up with "ler" in "Han ler" (He laughs), which is a form of "at le" (to laugh).

sentence.da: Man former skåle og krukker af vådt **ler**.
sentence.en: You shape bowls and jars from wet clay.

lesbisk.explanation: "Lesbisk" means "lesbian". It comes from the name of the Greek island Lesbos.

sentence.da: Hun bor sammen med sin kæreste, og de er et **lesbisk** par.
sentence.en: She lives with her partner, and they are a lesbian couple.

let.explanation: "Let" means "easy". To say a bag does not weigh much, use it for "light in weight": "en let taske" (a light bag).

sentence.da: En fjer er meget **let**.
sentence.en: A feather is very light.

letmælk.explanation: "Letmælk" means "low-fat milk". In Denmark, "letmælk" has 1.5% fat. It is built from "let" (light) and "mælk" (milk).

sentence.da: **Letmælk** har mindre fedt end sødmælk.
sentence.en: Low-fat milk has less fat than whole milk.

lettelse.explanation: "Lettelse" means "relief". To say something is a relief, say: "Det er en lettelse" (That is a relief). To say you feel relieved, use "lettet" (relieved): "Jeg er lettet" (I am relieved).

sentence.da: Jeg sukkede af **lettelse**, fordi prøven var slut.
sentence.en: I sighed with relief because the test was over.

lettere.explanation: "Lettere" means "easier". It comes from "let" (easy, light). To compare weight, it also means "lighter": "en lettere taske" (a lighter bag).

sentence.da: Min nye taske er **lettere** end den gamle.
sentence.en: My new bag is lighter than the old one.

lettet.explanation: "Lettet" means "relieved". To say what you are relieved about, use "over" (about): "Jeg er lettet over, at eksamen er overstået" (I am relieved that the exam is over).

sentence.da: Jeg var **lettet**, da hun ringede.
sentence.en: I was relieved when she called.

levedygtig.explanation: "Levedygtig" means "viable". It is built from "at leve" (to live) and "dygtig" (skilled). To say a company can keep going, say: "Firmaet er levedygtigt" (The company is viable).

sentence.da: Butikken er **levedygtig**, fordi den tjener flere penge, end den bruger.
sentence.en: The store is viable because it earns more money than it spends.

levende.explanation: "Levende" means "living". It comes from the verb "at leve" (to live). To say music is played live, use it for "live": "levende musik" (live music).

sentence.da: Kaninen ligger stille, men den er **levende**.
sentence.en: The rabbit lies still, but it is alive.

leverpostej.explanation: "Leverpostej" means "liver pâté". It is built from "lever" (liver) and "postej" (pâté). To talk about the warm kind, say: "lun leverpostej med bacon" (warm liver pâté with bacon).

sentence.da: Til frokost spiser jeg **leverpostej** på rugbrød.
sentence.en: For lunch I eat liver pâté on rye bread.

liberal.explanation: "Liberal" means "liberal". To describe a relaxed way of raising children, say: "en liberal opdragelse" (a relaxed upbringing).

sentence.da: Han er **liberal** og vil give folk mere frihed og mindre skat.
sentence.en: He is liberal and wants to give people more freedom and less tax.

lidenskab.explanation: "En lidenskab" means "a passion". To say you do something with great feeling, use "med lidenskab" (with passion): "Hun spiller med lidenskab" (She plays with passion).

sentence.da: Hans **lidenskab** er musik, og han spiller hver dag.
sentence.en: His passion is music, and he plays every day.

lidenskabelig.explanation: "Lidenskabelig" means "passionate". It is built from "en lidenskab" (a passion). To say someone cares deeply about a subject, say: "Hun har en lidenskabelig interesse for kunst" (She has a passionate interest in art).

sentence.da: Hun bliver **lidenskabelig**, når hun taler om musik.
sentence.en: She becomes passionate when she talks about music.

lidt.explanation: "Lidt" means "a little". To say you want a small amount of something, put it before the thing: "lidt mælk" (a little milk). To say you are slightly tired, put it before the describing word: "lidt træt" (a little tired). Do not mix it up with "lille" (small). For example, "en lille kop" (a small cup) is about size, while "lidt vand" (a little water) is about amount.

sentence.da: Jeg vil kun have **lidt** mad.
sentence.en: I only want a little food.

lidt efter lidt.explanation: "Lidt efter lidt" means "little by little". Literally, it is "a little after a little". To say how you learn a language, say: "Hun lærer dansk lidt efter lidt" (She learns Danish little by little).

forms.da: lidt efter lidt bliver det bedre
forms.en: little by little it gets better

sentence.da: **Lidt efter lidt** blev det lyst.
sentence.en: Little by little it got light.

lidt langsommere, tak.explanation: "Lidt langsommere, tak" means "a bit slower, please". "Langsommere" means "slower" and comes from "langsom" (slow). To ask someone to say it once more, ask: "Kan du sige det igen?" (Can you say that again?)

forms.en: Can you speak a bit slower?

sentence.da: Du taler for hurtigt. **Lidt langsommere, tak**!
sentence.en: You speak too fast. A bit slower, please!

lige.explanation: "Lige" means "straight". To point to the exact moment or place, it means "right": "lige nu" (right now) and "lige ved siden af" (right next to).

sentence.da: Stregen er meget **lige**.
sentence.en: The line is very straight.

lige meget hvad.explanation: "Lige meget hvad" means "no matter what". To promise someone help, say: "Jeg hjælper dig, lige meget hvad" (I will help you, no matter what). It is built from "lige meget" (it does not matter) and "hvad" (what).

forms.en: I am coming no matter what.

forms.da: Lige meget hvad der sker, ringer jeg.
forms.en: No matter what happens, I will call.

sentence.da: Jeg kommer, **lige meget hvad** der sker.
sentence.en: I will come, no matter what happens.

lige nu.explanation: "Lige nu" means "right now". It is built from "lige" (just) and "nu" (now). To say something happens in a little while instead, use "om lidt" (in a little while): "Jeg kommer om lidt" (I am coming in a little while).

forms.en: What are you doing right now?

sentence.da: Jeg har ikke tid **lige nu**.
sentence.en: I do not have time right now.

lige om lidt.explanation: "Lige om lidt" means "in just a moment". It is built from "om lidt" (in a little while) and "lige" (just).

forms.en: I am coming in just a moment.
We are leaving in just a moment.

sentence.da: Maden er klar **lige om lidt**.
sentence.en: The food will be ready in just a moment.

ligefrem.explanation: "Ligefrem" means "downright". To stress that something is very much so, put it before the describing word: "Det er ligefrem fantastisk" (It is downright fantastic). To say a person is direct and simple, use it for "straightforward": "en ligefrem mand" (a straightforward man).

sentence.da: Det er **ligefrem** utroligt, at han vandt uden at træne.
sentence.en: It is downright unbelievable that he won without training.

ligeglad.explanation: "Ligeglad" means "indifferent". To say you do not mind which choice is made, say: "Jeg er ligeglad" (I do not mind). To say someone does not care about other people, add "med" (about): "Han er ligeglad med andre" (He does not care about other people).

sentence.da: Jeg er **ligeglad**, om vi spiser pizza eller pasta.
sentence.en: I do not mind whether we eat pizza or pasta.

ligegyldig.explanation: "Ligegyldig" means "unimportant". To say something does not matter, say: "Det er ligegyldigt" (It makes no difference). To say a person does not care, use it for the person: "Hun virker ligegyldig" (She seems indifferent).

sentence.da: Han var **ligegyldig** og hørte ikke efter.
sentence.en: He was indifferent and did not listen.

ligeledes.explanation: "Ligeledes" means "likewise". To answer a greeting with the same, reply: "Rart at møde dig!" "Ligeledes!" (Nice to meet you! Likewise!)

forms.da: Han kommer, og det gør hun ligeledes
forms.en: He is coming, and so is she

sentence.da: Børn skal have tid til at lege, og voksne **ligeledes**.
sentence.en: Children need time to play, and so do adults.

ligesom.explanation: "Ligesom" means "just like". It is built from "lige" (just) and "som" (like). To compare two people, put it before the second one: "Hun er høj ligesom sin mor" (She is tall just like her mother).

forms.en: He is just like his father.

sentence.da: Du er **ligesom** din far.
sentence.en: You are just like your father.

ligestilling.explanation: "Ligestilling" means "equality". It is built from "lige" (equal) and "en stilling" (a position). To talk about equal treatment at work, say: "ligestilling på arbejdspladsen" (equality in the workplace).

sentence.da: **Ligestilling** betyder, at mænd og kvinder har de samme muligheder.
sentence.en: Equality means that men and women have the same opportunities.

ligeså.explanation: "Ligeså" means "just as". To say two things are equal, put it before the describing word: "Hun er ligeså høj som dig" (She is just as tall as you). You can also write it as two words with the same meaning: "lige så høj" (just as tall).

sentence.da: Min bror er **ligeså** høj som far, men meget tyndere.
sentence.en: My brother is just as tall as Dad, but much thinner.

ligeud.explanation: "Ligeud" means "straight ahead". To tell someone to go another way, use "til højre" (to the right) or "til venstre" (to the left): "Du skal til højre ved krydset" (You must go right at the intersection).

sentence.da: Ved krydset skal du ikke dreje, men gå **ligeud**.
sentence.en: At the intersection, do not turn, but go straight ahead.

ligeværdig.explanation: "Ligeværdig" means "equal". It is built from "lige" (equal) and "værd" (worth). To say two sides count the same, say: "Vi er ligeværdige parter" (We are equal parties).

sentence.da: I et godt forhold skal man føle sig **ligeværdig**.
sentence.en: In a good relationship you must feel equal.

lignende.explanation: "Lignende" means "similar". To say a problem is alike another one, put it before the noun: "et lignende problem" (a similar problem). To say one person looks like another, use "ligner" (looks like): "Han ligner sin far" (He looks like his father).

sentence.da: Jeg har haft et **lignende** problem før.
sentence.en: I have had a similar problem before.

lilla.explanation: "Lilla" means "purple". To say a lighter shade, put "lys" (light) in front of it: "lyslilla" (light purple).

sentence.da: Druer kan være grønne eller **lilla**.
sentence.en: Grapes can be green or purple.

lille.explanation: "Lille" means "small". To talk about more than one thing, use "små" (small), which looks different from "lille": "små biler" (small cars). To say someone is dear and little, say: "min lille ven" (my little friend).

sentence.da: Musen er meget **lille**.
sentence.en: The mouse is very small.

lim.explanation: "Lim" means "glue". The verb is "at lime" (to glue). For example, "Jeg limer billedet på papiret" (I glue the picture on the paper).

sentence.da: **Lim** holder to stykker papir sammen.
sentence.en: Glue holds two pieces of paper together.

linser.explanation: "Linser" means "lentils". To say one lentil, use "en linse": "Der ligger en linse på gulvet" (There is a lentil on the floor). The same word also means a lens. For example, "en kontaktlinse" (a contact lens).

sentence.da: Jeg laver suppe af røde **linser** og gulerødder.
sentence.en: I make soup from red lentils and carrots.

litteratur.explanation: "Litteratur" means "literature". To say all that has been written about a subject, add "om" (about): "litteraturen om søvn" (the literature on sleep).

sentence.da: **Litteratur** er for eksempel romaner, digte og skuespil.
sentence.en: Literature is, for example, novels, poems and plays.

livlig.explanation: "Livlig" means "lively". Do not mix it up with "levende" (alive). For example, "et levende dyr" (a living animal) is not dead, while "en livlig fest" (a lively party) is full of energy.

sentence.da: Gaden er **livlig** om aftenen, fordi mange restauranter har åbent.
sentence.en: The street is lively in the evening because many restaurants are open.

livsglæde.explanation: "En livsglæde" means "joy of life". It is built from "et liv" (a life) and "en glæde" (a joy). To say a person has it, use "livsglad" (full of joy of life): "Hun er livsglad" (She is full of joy of life).

sentence.da: Selv som gammel mand havde han en stor **livsglæde**.
sentence.en: Even as an old man he had a great zest for life.

livskvalitet.explanation: "Livskvalitet" means "quality of life". It is built from "et liv" (a life) and "en kvalitet" (a quality). To say a hobby makes your life better, say: "Hobbyen giver mig livskvalitet" (The hobby gives me quality of life).

sentence.da: Fritid giver mig **livskvalitet**, fordi jeg kan være sammen med familien.
sentence.en: Free time gives me quality of life because I can be with my family.

logik.explanation: "Logik" means "logic". To say there is a reason behind something, say: "Der er en logik i det" (There is logic in it). The describing word is "logisk" (logical).

sentence.da: Matematik bygger på **logik**, og hvert trin følger af det forrige.
sentence.en: Math is built on logic, and each step follows from the previous one.

logisk.explanation: "Logisk" means "logical". It comes from "en logik" (logic). To say something makes sense, say: "Det er helt logisk" (That is completely logical).

sentence.da: Det er **logisk**, fordi to plus to er fire.
sentence.en: It is logical, because two plus two is four.

lokal.explanation: "Lokal" means "local". To talk about news from your own town, say: "lokale nyheder" (local news).

sentence.da: Jeg køber mad hos en **lokal** bager.
sentence.en: I buy food from a local baker.

lokalt.explanation: "Lokalt" means "locally". It comes from "lokal" (local). To say you buy things in your own area, put it after the verb: "Jeg handler lokalt" (I shop locally).

sentence.da: Vi handler **lokalt**, fordi vi vil støtte byens bønder.
sentence.en: We shop locally because we want to support the town's farmers.

lommepenge.explanation: "Lommepenge" means "pocket money". It is built from "en lomme" (a pocket) and "penge" (money). The word "lomme" is also in "en lommelygte" (a flashlight). For example, "Jeg har en lommelygte i tasken" (I have a flashlight in my bag).

sentence.da: Min datter får hundrede kroner i **lommepenge**.
sentence.en: My daughter gets a hundred kroner in pocket money.

lotto.explanation: "Lotto" means "lotto". In Denmark, "Lotto" is run by the company "Danske Spil".

sentence.da: Han håber at vinde i **lotto** i weekenden.
sentence.en: He hopes to win at lotto this weekend.

lovende.explanation: "Lovende" means "promising". It comes from the verb "at love" (to promise). To say a person has talent, say: "Hun er et lovende talent" (She is a promising talent).

sentence.da: De første resultater af forsøget ser **lovende** ud.
sentence.en: The first results of the experiment look promising.

lovgivning.explanation: "Lovgivning" means "legislation". This word has no article, so leave out "en". For example, "Dansk lovgivning gælder for alle" (Danish legislation applies to everyone). It is built from "en lov" (a law) and "at give" (to give).

sentence.da: Ny **lovgivning** skal sikre, at alle børn kan komme i skole.
sentence.en: New legislation must ensure that all children can go to school.

lovlig.explanation: "Lovlig" means "legal". To say the opposite, put "u" in front: "ulovlig" (illegal). To say stealing is not allowed, say: "Det er ulovligt at stjæle" (It is illegal to steal).

sentence.da: Det er en **lovlig** handling, fordi loven tillader det.
sentence.en: It is a legal act, because the law allows it.

lovpligtig.explanation: "Lovpligtig" means "legally required". It is built from "en lov" (a law) and "pligtig" (obliged). To say a thing is required by law, say: "Cykellygter er lovpligtige" (Bike lights are required by law).

sentence.da: Alle bilister skal have en forsikring, fordi den er **lovpligtig**.
sentence.en: All drivers must have insurance because it is required by law.

loyal.explanation: "Loyal" means "loyal". To say who you are loyal to, add "over for" (towards): "Han er loyal over for sin chef" (He is loyal to his boss).

sentence.da: Han var **loyal** over for firmaet, selv da andre sagde op.
sentence.en: He was loyal to the company, even when others quit.

loyalitet.explanation: "Loyalitet" means "loyalty". The matching describing word is "loyal" (loyal). For example, "en loyal ven" (a loyal friend).

sentence.da: **Loyalitet** er, at man støtter sine venner, også når det er svært.
sentence.en: Loyalty is when you support your friends, even when it is hard.

luft.explanation: "Luft" means "air". To say something is in the air, say: "Fuglen er i luften" (The bird is in the air). It is also the first part of "en lufthavn" (an airport), literally "an air harbor".

sentence.da: Vi åbner vinduet for frisk **luft**.
sentence.en: We open the window for fresh air.

lukket.explanation: "Lukket" means "closed". It comes from the verb "at lukke" (to close). To say a shop is not open, say: "Butikken er lukket" (The shop is closed).

sentence.da: Døren er **lukket**, men vinduet er åbent.
sentence.en: The door is closed, but the window is open.

luksus.explanation: "Luksus" means "luxury". To talk about something nice you do not need, say: "Et langt bad er luksus" (A long bath is a luxury).

sentence.da: Det er **luksus** at sove længe i weekenden.
sentence.en: It is a luxury to sleep in on the weekend.

lummer.explanation: "Lummer" means "muggy". For weather, use the form "lummert": "Vejret er lummert" (The weather is muggy). To say the weather is only hot, use "varm" (warm): "Det er en varm dag" (It is a warm day).

sentence.da: Luften er **lummer**, og der kommer nok tordenvejr snart.
sentence.en: The air is muggy, and a thunderstorm is probably coming soon.

lun.explanation: "Lun" means "cozy". To say food or drink is nicely warm, use it for "warm": "lun suppe" (warm soup). To say someone has a gently dry sense of humor, say: "Han har en lun humor" (He has a gentle sense of humor).

sentence.da: Stuen er **lun**, fordi brændeovnen har brændt hele dagen.
sentence.en: The room is cozy because the wood stove has burned all day.

ly.explanation: "Et ly" means "a shelter". To say you find a place to stay dry, say: "De fandt ly under et tag" (They found shelter under a roof). To say something happens hidden by darkness, use "i ly af mørket" (under cover of darkness): "Han sneg sig ind i ly af mørket" (He sneaked in under cover of darkness).

sentence.da: Vi løb ind under et træ for at finde **ly** for regnen.
sentence.en: We ran under a tree to find shelter from the rain.

lydig.explanation: "Lydig" means "obedient". To say the opposite, put "u" in front: "ulydig" (disobedient): "Hunden er ulydig" (The dog is disobedient).

sentence.da: Hunden er **lydig** og sætter sig, når jeg siger det.
sentence.en: The dog is obedient and sits down when I say so.

lydløs.explanation: "Lydløs" means "silent". To say a phone is on silent mode, say: "Min telefon er på lydløs" (My phone is on silent). The ending "-løs" means "without", as in "hjælpeløs" (helpless). To say a person says nothing, use "tavs" (silent): "en tavs mand" (a silent man).

sentence.da: Elbilen er næsten **lydløs**, når den kører langsomt.
sentence.en: The electric car is almost silent when it drives slowly.

lykke.explanation: "Lykke" means "happiness". To say money cannot buy it, say: "Penge giver ikke lykke" (Money does not bring happiness). To wish someone luck, say: "Lykke til!" (Good luck!)

sentence.da: Jeg ønsker dig al **lykke** i dit nye hjem.
sentence.en: I wish you all happiness in your new home.

lykkelig.explanation: "Lykkelig" means "happy". It comes from "en lykke" (happiness). To say what makes you happy, add "med" (with): "Jeg er lykkelig med mit liv" (I am happy with my life).

sentence.da: Hun er **lykkelig** med sit nye job.
sentence.en: She is happy with her new job.

lyn.explanation: "Et lyn" means "a flash of lightning". It is the first part of "en lynlås" (a zipper), built from "et lyn" and "en lås" (a lock). To say something is very fast, use "lynhurtig" (lightning fast): "Bilen er lynhurtig" (The car is lightning fast).

sentence.da: Man ser **lyn** først og hører torden bagefter.
sentence.en: You see lightning first and hear thunder afterward.

lyng.explanation: "Lyng" means "heather". In Denmark, heather grows on a heath, "en hede". For example, "Lyngen blomstrer på heden" (The heather blooms on the heath).

sentence.da: På heden vokser der **lyng**, og den blomstrer lilla.
sentence.en: On the heath there grows heather, and it blooms purple.

lys.explanation: "Lys" means "bright". To say someone has fair hair, use the form "lyst": "Han har lyst hår" (He has fair hair). There is also a different word "et lys", which means "a candle". For example, "Tænd et lys" (Light a candle).

sentence.da: Stuen er meget **lys** i dag.
sentence.en: The living room is very bright today.

lyseblå.explanation: "Lyseblå" means "light blue". It is built from "lyse-" (light) and "blå" (blue). To say the darker shade, put "mørke-" (dark) in front of "blå" instead: "mørkeblå" (dark blue).

sentence.da: Himlen er **lyseblå** i dag.
sentence.en: The sky is light blue today.

lysegrøn.explanation: "Lysegrøn" means "light green". It is built from "lyse-" (light) and "grøn" (green). To say the darker shade, put "mørke-" (dark) in front of "grøn" instead: "en mørkegrøn jakke" (a dark green jacket).

sentence.da: Salaten er **lysegrøn**.
sentence.en: The lettuce is light green.

lysende.explanation: "Lysende" means "bright". It comes from the verb "at lyse" (to shine). To say a color is very strong, put it before the color: "lysende gul" (bright yellow).

sentence.da: Fyrtårnet er **lysende** og viser skibene vej i mørket.
sentence.en: The lighthouse is bright and shows the ships the way in the dark.

lyserød.explanation: "Lyserød" means "pink". It is built from "lys" (light) and "rød" (red), so literally it is "light red".

sentence.da: Grisen er **lyserød**.
sentence.en: The pig is pink.

lyshåret.explanation: "Lyshåret" means "fair-haired". It is built from "lys" (light) and "hår" (hair). To say someone has dark hair instead, say: "Hun har mørkt hår" (She has dark hair).

sentence.da: Hendes bror er **lyshåret**, men hun selv har mørkt hår.
sentence.en: Her brother is fair-haired, but she herself has dark hair.

læder.explanation: "Læder" means "leather". To say a bag is not real leather, use "kunstlæder" (faux leather): "en taske af kunstlæder" (a bag made of faux leather).

sentence.da: **Læder** laves af huden fra en ko.
sentence.en: Leather is made from the skin of a cow.

lækker.explanation: "Lækker" means "delicious". To say something looks great, use it for "great-looking": "en lækker bil" (a great-looking car). Before a plural noun, the "k" is dropped. For example, "lækre kager" (delicious cakes).

sentence.da: Kagen er meget **lækker**.
sentence.en: The cake is really delicious.

længe.explanation: "Længe" means "for a long time". To ask how long, say: "Hvor længe bliver du?" (How long are you staying?). To say something was long ago, say: "for længe siden" (a long time ago): "Vi mødtes for længe siden" (We met a long time ago). Do not mix it up with "lang" (long). For example, "en lang vej" (a long road).

sentence.da: Jeg har ventet **længe** på bussen.
sentence.en: I have waited a long time for the bus.

længst.explanation: "Længst" means "furthest". To ask who lives the furthest away, say: "Hvem bor længst væk?" (Who lives the furthest away?) For time, it also means "longest": "Hvem har boet her længst?" (Who has lived here the longest?)

sentence.da: Min bror bor **længst** fra os.
sentence.en: My brother lives the furthest from us.

læseforståelse.explanation: "Læseforståelse" means "reading comprehension". It is built from "at læse" (to read) and "en forståelse" (an understanding). To say you practise it, say: "Vi træner læseforståelse i dansktimerne" (We practise reading comprehension in the Danish lessons).

sentence.da: Ved en test i **læseforståelse** svarer eleverne på spørgsmål om en tekst.
sentence.en: In a test of reading comprehension, the students answer questions about a text.

løbende.explanation: "Løbende" means "ongoing". To say you do something again and again over time, put it after the verb: "Vi opdaterer siden løbende" (We update the page on an ongoing basis). It comes from "at løbe" (to run). For example, "løbende vand" (running water).

sentence.da: Vi tjekker priserne **løbende**, fordi de ændrer sig hver uge.
sentence.en: We check the prices continuously because they change every week.

lørdag.explanation: "En lørdag" means "a Saturday". To say something happens on the coming Saturday, use "på lørdag" (on Saturday): "Vi ses på lørdag" (See you on Saturday). To say it happens every Saturday, use "om lørdagen" (on Saturdays): "Om lørdagen sover jeg længe" (On Saturdays I sleep in).

sentence.da: Vi har fri på **lørdag**.
sentence.en: We are off on Saturday.

løs.explanation: "Løs" means "loose". To say a dog is off its leash, say: "Hunden er løs" (The dog is loose).

sentence.da: Min tand er **løs**, og den falder snart ud.
sentence.en: My tooth is loose, and it will fall out soon.

løvfald.explanation: "Et løvfald" means "leaf fall". It is built from "løv" (the leaves on trees) and "et fald" (a fall). To say trees lose their leaves, say: "Træerne mister løvet" (The trees lose their leaves). To say one leaf, use "et blad" (a leaf): "Der ligger et blad på bordet" (There is a leaf on the table).

sentence.da: Efter **løvfald** ligger bladene tykt på jorden.
sentence.en: After leaf fall the leaves lie thick on the ground.
